title: Baseline retest for cores/bench
Share a radix-4 combinational divider across RV32M divide and remainder
motivation:
The baseline's worst timed path is 199.837 ns across 156 cells and passes
through forwarding and the combinational ALU. Its 5.442 MHz Fmax strongly
suggests that the deeply unrolled divide/remainder arithmetic dominates
fitness. alu.sv currently expresses signed and unsigned division and
remainder separately. Improving this timed arithmetic cone can increase
CoreMark iterations/second without changing instruction throughput or
adding pipeline control under the approximately 22% memory stalls.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace only the real DIV, DIVU, REM, and REMU implementations with one
shared, fully combinational unsigned radix-4 restoring divmod network.
Convert operands to unsigned magnitudes for signed DIV/REM, run sixteen
dependent steps that consume two dividend bits and emit two quotient
bits each, then apply the quotient and remainder signs. Each step forms
T = {previous_remainder[31:0], next_dividend_pair}, computes T-D, T-2D,
and T-3D in parallel, and chooses the largest nonnegative trial. Derive
both each trial's borrow and its candidate remainder from the same
subtraction; avoid a serial comparator followed by a second subtractor.
Precompute the 34-bit D, 2D, and 3D once. Use 35-bit zero-extended trial
subtractions so bit 34 indicates borrow, and retain only the selected
low 32 remainder bits between steps: for nonzero D the restored
remainder is always less than D. Let ok1, ok2, and ok3 denote the three
no-borrow predicates. The quotient digit is {ok2, ok3 | (ok1 & !ok2)};
select the remainder with mutually exclusive masks !ok1,
ok1 & !ok2, ok2 & !ok3, and ok3 applied to T and the three trial results.
Use parallel masked-OR selection to avoid a serial priority mux chain.
Assemble the sixteen base-4 digits
into the 32-bit quotient. This reduces the number of dependent divider
steps from thirty-two to sixteen and shares the expensive network
across quotient/remainder and signed/unsigned operations.

Keep the alu module interface, zero-cycle combinational latency,
multiplication, RV32I operations, forwarding, stall handling, pipeline
registers, decoder legality, and nret=1 contract intact. Preserve every
RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS expression exactly. Explicitly return all ones for
division by zero and the original dividend for remainder by zero;
preserve DIV(INT_MIN,-1)=INT_MIN and REM(INT_MIN,-1)=0. Signed remainder
takes only the dividend's sign. Do not introduce FPGA-specific divider
primitives or change the evaluation flow. The expected gain comes from
shortening the existing arithmetic path, with no extra CoreMark cycles.

changes.description:
Replace the real / and % expressions for the four RV32M divide and
remainder operations with one shared sixteen-step radix-4 unsigned
divmod network, explicit widened parallel trial subtractions, signed
magnitude preprocessing and result sign correction, and architectural
corner-case selection. Leave ALTOPS and other ALU operations unchanged.

Extend exact-result division/remainder vectors with all four radix-4
quotient digits, divisors near 2^30, 2^31, and 2^32, unsigned quotients
with bit 31 set, sign combinations, dividend smaller than divisor,
zero divisors, and INT_MIN/-1. Use independent integer divmod on
magnitudes to check randomized DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU results, including
quotient/remainder identity modulo 2^32 and remainder magnitude bounds
for nonzero divisors, so the signed overflow case is handled correctly.

title: Replace combinational division with a bounded multicycle EX divider
motivation:
The sole recorded experiment is the baseline: fitness 12.12, median Fmax
5.442 MHz, 12312 LUT4s, and a 199.837 ns path with 156 cells through
forwarding, EX, and the ALU. There are no prior structural attempts or
LESSONS.md. The ALU currently computes signed and unsigned division and
remainder with combinational / and % operators. These long arithmetic
chains constrain the clock even when the executing instruction is an
ordinary integer operation. Sharing and registering division should
substantially improve frequency and reduce LUT pressure at the cost of
extra cycles only for DIV, DIVU, REM, and REMU. Multiplication remains
on its existing path, preserving throughput in CoreMark's matrix loops.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Move DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU out of the combinational EX result path into one
registered, unsigned-magnitude quotient/remainder engine. Use a restoring
shift/subtract recurrence with eight quotient bits computed per clock:
eight bit steps are unrolled combinationally and reused for four clocks,
rather than cascading all 32 steps in one clock. Register operand
magnitudes and sign flags at launch, then restore quotient sign from
rs1-sign XOR rs2-sign and remainder sign from rs1. Reserve at most seven
clocks from accepted launch to result availability, including setup and
sign restoration; keep the zero-wait retirement gap within the unchanged
ten-cycle liveness window, including pipeline transfer cycles. Use the
same bounded handshake latency in ALTOPS mode, substituting only the
arithmetic value with the exact existing formal formulas. Do not hide a
slow real divider behind a faster formal-only completion path.

Launch exactly once for a valid legal divide in ID/EX when the older MEM
instruction can advance. Capture the forwarded operands and their RVFI
values before holding the instruction, since forwarding sources can
disappear while older instructions drain. Hold PC and ID/EX during the
operation; allow older EX/MEM and MEM/WB instructions to drain once,
inserting EX/MEM bubbles instead of repeatedly issuing the old instruction.
Existing dmem backpressure must still hold an outstanding memory request.
Retain a completed division result until EX/MEM accepts it, then publish
it exactly once through the normal forwarding, writeback, and single
channel RVFI paths. Qualify redirects and side effects with valid and
actual stage advance so stalls cannot replay a branch or memory request.

Preserve the existing alu unit-test interface with a constant elaboration
parameter if needed: its default may retain combinational divide for
standalone tests, but the core must instantiate the no-combinational-divide
variant. No / or % hardware may remain reachable in the timed core.
Implement all RV32M divide-by-zero and INT_MIN/-1 results exactly, reset
the engine cleanly, and preserve nret=1, decoder legality, memory handshakes,
retirement order, and every existing correctness check. Add tests of the
actual iterative engine and its pipeline integration, not just the legacy
combinational arithmetic. The prediction is that reduced divider depth
outweighs its added dynamic cycles; compare vendor Fmax times bracketed
CoreMark iterations/cycle, with canonical CRCs and random bus stalls.

title: Fetch-time bimodal prediction removes taken-branch bubbles
motivation:
The current core always fetches PC+4 and flushes the younger instruction
on every taken conditional branch or jump, even for stable CoreMark loop
branches. IF/ID is combinational, so steering the PC when an instruction
is accepted into ID/EX can supply its predicted successor without adding
a pipeline stage. A small direction-only predictor avoids a tagged target
array and should reduce benchmark cycles while leaving the dominant
combinational M-extension timing path structurally unchanged. The local
history has only the baseline and no prior predictor attempts or lessons.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one compact fetch-time control-flow predictor: a 64-entry bimodal
branch-history table of two-bit saturating counters, indexed by PC[7:2]
and reset to weakly not taken (01). Predecode only legal RV32I conditional
branches and JAL from the raw fetched instruction. For a conditional
branch, use the counter MSB as the direction; predict JAL taken without
consulting the table. Form direct targets from PC plus the B/J immediate,
and predict only word-aligned targets. All other instructions, including
JALR, predict PC+4. Keep direction state only: no BTB, global history,
return stack, target cache, or instruction buffering.

Carry the exact predicted next PC with each accepted instruction through
IF/ID and ID/EX. In EX compute the existing architecturally resolved next
PC, including the existing sequential-next-PC behavior on alignment
traps. Redirect and flush the younger instruction only when this resolved
next PC differs from the prediction, gated by ID/EX.valid and EX acceptance
(!stall_ex_mem). A predicted-taken branch that resolves not taken must
redirect to its own PC+4. Correctly predicted control transfers must not
flush or redirect. RVFI pc_wdata remains the actual resolved next PC and
JAL/JALR link writes remain PC+4.

Train a conditional branch's indexed counter toward its actual outcome
exactly once when the valid, legal, aligned branch advances from EX into
EX/MEM. Never train held EX instructions, bubbles, jumps, or trapped
branches. Predictor lookup is combinational and updates are synchronous;
same-index fetch/update may use the pre-update counter, since the chosen
next PC is captured with the instruction. A prediction changes the fetch
PC only when fetch/decode acceptance is enabled. Reset overrides all PC
updates; an accepted EX misprediction overrides fetch stall; otherwise
load-use, imem, and dmem stalls hold the PC and preserve held prediction
metadata. Suppress EX correction while an older MEM access stalls, then
perform its correction and table update once on release. Preserve the
current forwarding and held MEM/WB behavior, decode legality, trap
semantics, single-channel RVFI interface, and all evaluation contracts.

Validate with directed prediction/recovery cases and randomized imem and
dmem stalls, the existing unit/formal/cosim gates, and canonical CoreMark
CRCs and marker-bracketed cycles. Measure final fitness using median Gowin
Fmax times CoreMark iterations/cycle; the prediction expects a cycle-count
reduction rather than an arithmetic timing improvement.

changes.description:
Own the 64x2 direction table and its EX training interface. Predecode
legal conditional branches and JAL from raw imem_data, generate aligned
direct targets, select the predicted successor, and emit its exact PC
in the fetch bundle. Advance to this successor only on fetch acceptance;
retain reset, stall holding, and accepted-recovery priority. Keep table
size fixed and small so lookup stays off the long arithmetic path.

Add a 32-bit predicted_next_pc field to if_id_t and id_ex_t. Preserve
the architectural EX/MEM and MEM/WB pc_next fields and retirement width.

Capture predicted_next_pc with pc/instr/valid; retain it on ID/EX hold
and clear it with the existing bubble/reset path. Keep decoder defaults
and all operand/control fields unchanged.

Share the existing actual-next-PC calculation between RVFI propagation
and prediction comparison. Emit correction only for a valid instruction
advancing out of EX whose actual successor differs from its captured
prediction; correction target is the actual successor, including PC+4
for not-taken recovery or alignment trap. Export accepted, nontrapping
conditional-branch PC and actual outcome for one synchronous BHT update.
Preserve forwarded operands, JALR bit clearing, traps, and link values.

Wire the EX branch-training signals back to IF and keep redirect wired
as the sole correction/flush event. Use the existing dmem-derived EX
acceptance signal to prevent repeated training and correction on holds.
Preserve all top-level ports and the nret=1 RVFI contract.

Treat redirect as an accepted misprediction correction, rather than
every taken transfer. Preserve load-use bubbles, bus stall priorities,
and MEM/WB forwarding retention; correct predictions create no flush.

Add directed checks for counter saturation/training, loop warmup and
exit, forward taken and not-taken branches, PC-index aliasing, predicted
JAL and unresolved JALR, misaligned targets, and non-control/illegal
encodings. Exercise load-use plus prediction and consecutive/random
imem/dmem holds, including a MEM stall with a branch in EX. Check exact
retired PCs, architectural results, strict RVFI order, absence of
wrong-path stores, and no duplicate correction or counter update.

title: Shorten the registered divider with four parallel-trial radix-4 steps
motivation:
The current champion scores 71.55 at 32.136 MHz. Its worst vendor-timed
path is 36.356 ns across 249 cells, entirely within u_ex/u_div, from a
divisor register to a remainder register. The engine currently cascades
eight dependent 33-bit restoring subtract/select steps in each RUN
clock. This arithmetic chain limits the clock for every instruction.
The earlier fully combinational radix-4 attempt still had sixteen
dependent digit steps and gained only 9.90% over the original baseline;
this proposal instead optimizes the champion's existing registered
engine, which has only eight quotient bits to compute per clock.
Reducing its dependent arithmetic depth without adding cycles directly
targets the measured bottleneck and preserves the fixed liveness bound.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the eight radix-2 restoring steps in each div_unit RUN clock
with four radix-4 steps, each producing two quotient bits. Preserve the
existing launch, four RUN clocks, one SIGN clock, and held DONE result
schedule exactly in both real and RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS builds. This is a
local arithmetic rewrite: the pipeline and divider handshake keep their
current behavior, and CoreMark instruction throughput should stay the
same while the divider's register-to-register path becomes shorter.

At launch capture the unsigned divisor magnitude D and the widened
multiples 2D and 3D. All multiples must be 34 bits; form 3D with an
explicitly widened addition during launch rather than recomputing it
inside the RUN recurrence. Each digit step forms the 34-bit trial
T = {remainder[31:0], quotient[31:30]}. Compute T-D, T-2D, and T-3D in
parallel as 35-bit zero-extended subtractions. Their bit 34 supplies
borrow, so no separate compare followed by subtract is needed. With
ok1, ok2, and ok3 denoting no-borrow for D, 2D, and 3D respectively,
append the quotient digit {ok2, ok3 | (ok1 & !ok2)}. Select the low
32 remainder bits using disjoint masks !ok1, ok1 & !ok2,
ok2 & !ok3, and ok3 on T and the three difference results. Express
selection as parallel masked OR, avoiding a serial priority mux chain.
Shift the quotient left by two per digit and register the fourth step
after each RUN clock. For D nonzero, the restored remainder is below D,
so storing 32 remainder bits is sufficient. For D zero, every digit is
three and the final remainder is the original dividend magnitude.

Retain the existing signed-magnitude preprocessing, quotient and
remainder sign flags, separate sign-restoration clock, reset behavior,
and consume semantics. Division by zero must return all ones; remainder
by zero must return the original dividend; DIV(INT_MIN,-1) must return
INT_MIN and REM(INT_MIN,-1) must return zero. Keep all existing ALTOPS
formulas and their five-clock latency, top-level nret=1 ports, decoder
legality, RVFI ordering, memory stall behavior, and correctness checks.
The launch path through magnitude and multiple generation must also be
checked in vendor timing; moving the bottleneck there would defeat the
expected gain. Evaluate the median Gowin Fmax times marker-bracketed
CoreMark iterations/cycle with the existing random stalls and CRC gates.

title: Fold the divider to five bit steps per clock with a fused final partial group
motivation:
The current champion reaches fitness 71.55 at 32.136 MHz, but its worst
Gowin path is now entirely inside u_ex/u_div: divisor_q to remainder_q,
36.356 ns and 249 cells. Eight dependent 33-bit restoring subtract/mux
steps remain between registers. The prior structural change removed
combinational division and improved fitness by 490.35%; its measured
bracketed CoreMark cycle count remained exactly 4,491,485, matching the
baseline. That is evidence that additional divider latency has little
cost in this workload, whereas divider timing still limits every cycle.
The combinational radix-4 attempt improved the baseline clock only 9.9%,
so the promising next structural move is a shorter registered recurrence.
LESSONS.md is absent; the recorded structural history contains only the
successful bounded multicycle divider. The unchanged ten-cycle liveness
window prevents simply using a much slower bit-serial engine.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Restructure only the shared divider's sequential datapath from four
groups of eight restoring bit steps to six groups of five steps and
one final group of two steps. Reuse one physical chain of five 33-bit
subtract/restore cells and register quotient and remainder after each
full five-bit group. Widen the group counter to three bits. Keep
operand-magnitude and sign capture at the accepted launch edge. This
cuts the recurring arithmetic depth from eight cells to five and
reduces divisor fanout and replicated divider logic.

Remove the separate SIGN state. On the seventh RUN edge, form the
registered result directly from quotient_step[2] and remainder_step[2],
applying the captured quotient or remainder sign and operation selection
before entering DONE. Use the final combinational step outputs, not the
old quotient_q/remainder_q values, and do not execute three padding
steps after processing all 32 dividend bits. Compute quotient and
remainder sign corrections in parallel, then select the requested
result. The terminal path contains only two restoring steps plus sign
correction, keeping it shorter than the five-step recurring path.
An accepted launch at edge L must assert result_valid immediately after
edge L+7; DONE retains the registered result until consume. With the
existing EX launch/transfer protocol, consecutive divides have a
nine-cycle zero-wait RVFI retirement gap; the extra recovery cycle for
a taken branch followed by a divide still fits the ten-cycle limit.
Preserve that bound and the existing formal liveness configuration.

Give real arithmetic and RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS precisely the same seven-RUN
schedule. ALTOPS still captures the exact existing subtraction/XOR
formula and publishes it only on the seventh RUN edge. Preserve all
signed/unsigned quotient and remainder results, including zero divisors
and INT_MIN/-1. Retain the existing rule that quotient sign inversion
is disabled for divisor zero, and that signed remainder follows only
the dividend sign. Keep start/busy/result_valid/consume ports, captured
forwarded operands and RVFI metadata, completed-result retention,
reset cancellation, and single publication through EX/MEM unchanged.
The core must still elaborate the divide-disabled combinational ALU.

This is one structural folding and retiming change. Its expected fitness
gain comes from reducing the measured divider register-to-register path,
with two additional execution clocks only on divide/remainder
instructions. The final sign path or the existing multiplier may become
the next clock limit, so a twofold Fmax increase is not assumed. Validate
exact arithmetic and identical real/ALTOPS completion schedules, all
existing formal/cosim checks, the unchanged ten-cycle retirement bound,
and canonical CoreMark CRCs under random memory stalls. Score the final
circuit with median Gowin Fmax times marker-bracketed iterations/cycle.

changes.description:

implementation_notes:
# Five-step folded divider with fused final group

## Implementation

- Replaced the eight-cell restoring chain with one shared five-cell chain.
  The three-bit group counter runs six full five-bit groups, followed by
  a two-bit terminal group: exactly 32 dividend bits and seven RUN edges.
- Removed SIGN. On RUN group six, parallel quotient/remainder sign
  corrections use quotient_step[2] and remainder_step[2], then select and
  register the requested result. The terminal edge does not update the
  arithmetic registers from step five or process padding bits.
- Accepted launch at edge L produces result_valid immediately after L+7
  in both real arithmetic and RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS. The existing ALTOPS
  subtraction/XOR formulas remain captured at launch and published only
  at completion.
- Preserved operand/sign capture, zero-divisor quotient sign suppression,
  dividend-only remainder sign, INT_MIN/-1 behavior, DONE retention,
  rejected starts, consume/next-start support, and reset cancellation.
- EX's implementation and RVFI routing are unchanged; only its latency
  comment changed. No core IO, retirement width, or formal settings changed.

## Tests and deviations

- Divider tests check result_valid on every RUN edge, exercise early
  consumes and rejected starts, retained results, simultaneous consume
  and relaunch, and reset in all seven RUN groups plus DONE. Both builds
  exercise 1,764 directed/random arithmetic cases with an independent
  oracle, including every final low-bit pair and both operand signs.
- EX tests cover stalls beginning before and after completion, forwarded
  operand/payload capture, all reset phases, no duplicate publication,
  and REM(-10, 3), whose remainder changes in the final pair.
- Pipeline tests add 48 consecutive divide/remainder instructions with
  dependencies and x0 destinations, and BEQ/JAL/JALR targets beginning
  with divides. They verify exact nine-cycle consecutive-divide gaps and
  ten-cycle redirect-to-divide gaps without relaxing the existing bound.
  Directed nine-clock memory stalls and seeded 22% random stalls retain
  strict RVFI order, source/result checks, and exact memory side effects.
- The pipeline test runner needed an explicit RTL include path to find
  core_pkg.sv from its build directory. Fixed only test_pipeline.py;
  shared helpers and protected build files are unchanged.
- Bench declares nret: 1. Plain make cosim defaulted its C++ harness to
  NRET=2 and failed compilation; rerunning with NRET=1 used the existing
  contract correctly. No RTL or harness changes were needed.

## Local validation

- Real and ALTOPS Verilator lint: pass, no warnings.
- Formal: PASS on the first RTL attempt, 53 passed / 0 failed. Command:
  RTL_DIR=cores/bench/rtl CORE_NAME=bench JOBS=8 bash formal/run_all.sh.
  This includes liveness and unique with the unchanged ten-cycle window.
  No formal counterexample or fix retry occurred.
- All eight pytest runners pass across the suite run and the corrected
  pipeline rerun; all 93 cocotb cases pass.
- NRET=1 make cosim TARGET=bench: pass. Selftest RVFI comparisons pass
  with zero-wait and random imem/dmem stalls. CoreMark under random
  stalls passes canonical CRCs e9f5/e714/1fd7/8e3a/fcaf and the validation
  literal, completes at EBREAK, and makes no out-of-bounds access.
- make timing TARGET=bench: pass.
- NRET=1 make fpga TARGET=bench: pass, all three placements fit.

## Measured score

- Gowin Fmax for placement options 0/1/2: 45.414 / 48.625 / 48.625 MHz.
- Median Fmax: 48.625 MHz, versus 32.136 MHz before (+51.31%).
- Marker-bracketed CoreMark cycles: 4,491,485 for 10 iterations, exactly
  matching the prior champion. Iterations/cycle: 10 / 4,491,485.
- Fitness: 108.26 iterations/second, versus 71.55 before (+51.31%).
- Logic: 2,822; registers: 643; LUT-RAM: 8; BSRAM: 6; DSP: 6.
- Placement option 0's worst divider path is divisor_q -> remainder_q,
  27.286 ns and 109 cells, versus 36.356 ns and 249 cells before. It is
  now fourth in that placement's setup report. The worst overall path
  is register-file -> ID/EX through forwarding/control, 27.314 ns.

## Concerns

No functional issue remains from local checks. The full arithmetic
formal-deep suite was not run; arithmetic was checked by the independent
divider oracle, the combinational ALU suite, pipeline models, and cosim.
Forwarding/control and routing now compete with the shorter divider path
for the clock limit, so further divider folding alone may have less gain.

title: PC-only tagged target prediction for branches and indirect jumps
motivation:
The champion is the multicycle-divider core, with fitness 71.55,
32.136 MHz median Fmax and 4,491,485 bracketed CoreMark cycles. There
is no LESSONS.md. The previous predictor attempt, hyp-20261004-003-r1s2,
passed formal and cosim and reduced cycles to 4,201,766, but used the
old combinational-divider parent: its 5.292 MHz Fmax produced only
3.88% improvement over that baseline, below the 4.6% acceptance margin.
That result supports the cycle-saving opportunity without establishing
the timing cost on the present champion. It predicted direct branches
and JAL from fetched instruction bits and did not predict JALR.
CoreMark contains recurrent loop branches, calls and indirect control
transfers. Learning their destinations in a small tagged target table
can avoid the current one-bubble redirect while keeping instruction
decoding and immediate addition out of the fetch-PC prediction path.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one 64-entry, direct-mapped, PC-only branch-target predictor to
the existing single-issue core. Index with PC[7:2]; each entry holds
a valid bit, the full remaining PC tag [31:8], a word-aligned target
[31:2], a conditional/unconditional bit and a two-bit saturating
conditional direction counter. A matching unconditional entry predicts
its target; a matching conditional entry predicts its target only when
the counter MSB is one. A miss or not-taken prediction selects PC+4.
Include legal JAL and JALR as unconditional entries, using the last
resolved JALR target. This is one target-prediction mechanism; retain
the existing divider, ALU, pipeline depth and memory organization.
Lookup must depend only on the registered fetch PC and table state,
with no imem_data decoding, immediate adder or EX-to-IF combinational
training bypass. Keep full tags and full architectural target bits;
do not assume the program occupies a particular address range.

Reset only valid bits to make all entries miss; payload arrays need
not reset and must never influence prediction without a valid tag hit.
Use an asynchronous lookup and synchronous EX updates, with old-state
behavior for a simultaneous lookup/update of the same entry. Prefer
compact inferred distributed storage for tags/targets where supported,
and a small separate counter bank. Do not introduce a registered table
read or an additional fetch cycle. Do not add global history, a return
stack, instruction caching or unrelated timing optimizations.

Carry the exact chosen predicted_next_pc with every accepted fetch
into ID/EX. On an actual EX instruction transfer, compare it with the
architectural next PC already computed for RVFI. Recover and flush
the younger instruction only on a mismatch, including taken-to-not-
taken recovery to the branch's own PC+4 and changed indirect targets.
A correct prediction must allow the successor into ID/EX in the same
cycle that its predecessor advances. Retain link values PC+4, JALR
bit-zero clearing and all current alignment-trap behavior. RVFI must
report the actual resolved next PC, never the predictor's guess.

Apply mismatch detection to every valid accepted instruction, even a
non-control or illegal instruction at a PC with stale predictor state:
its actual successor is PC+4 under the existing trap convention.
Trapped branch/jump targets also recover to the existing sequential
successor. A divide may only recover when its result is consumed,
using the prediction captured with the held divide, never at launch
or during busy cycles. Suppress recovery and training during an older
stalled MEM access. Accepted recovery overrides an imem stall; reset
overrides recovery. Otherwise fetch advances to its predicted PC only
when decode accepts the valid instruction. Load-use, division wait and
dmem stalls hold the PC and ID/EX prediction metadata as appropriate.

Train exactly once per valid legal nontrapping control transfer from
EX to EX/MEM. Allocate conditional branches even when not taken, storing
their direct branch target rather than their sequential successor.
Initialize a replacement entry's counter to weakly taken (10) for a
taken branch or weakly not taken (01) for a not-taken branch; thereafter
saturate toward the actual direction on tag/type matches. Allocate JAL
and JALR with the actual resolved target and unconditional type; refresh
indirect targets on each accepted resolution. Never train bubbles,
held instructions or trapped targets. Invalidate a matching stale entry
when an accepted instruction is non-control or traps; correctness must
not depend on static instruction contents at a previously learned PC.
Do not retain speculative predictor updates that require rollback.

The prior direct predictor's cycle reduction alone corresponds to
about 6.9% throughput improvement at unchanged Fmax. The hypothesis
expects roughly 10% fitness improvement from comparable direct-transfer
savings plus learned JALR targets, with medium confidence because tag
conflicts, changing return targets and placement overhead may reduce
that gain. The current limiting path is inside the registered divider;
the small PC-only lookup should remain below that delay. Acceptance
must use measured median Gowin Fmax times marker-bracketed iterations
per cycle, with all existing correctness gates and canonical CRCs.

title: Remove load-use bubbles with ready-qualified MEM-to-EX forwarding
motivation: The champion scores 108.26 at 48.625 MHz with 4,491,485 bracketed CoreMark cycles. The successful five-step divider leaves several competing arithmetic and control timing paths. Previous micro_opt radix-4 trials did not beat this champion, and local control-mux experiments failed to clear the 4.6 percent acceptance threshold. LESSONS.md is absent. A throughput improvement is therefore more promising than another small clock-only change. The current hazard unit always inserts a bubble behind a dependent load because EX/MEM forwarding exposes only the effective address. The memory interface actually supplies load data combinationally during MEM, and dmem backpressure already holds the dependent EX instruction until the load can complete.

Add one local MEM-to-EX forwarding path for completed loads, preserving the pipeline stages and retirement schedule for all other instructions. Expose the existing mem_stage sign/zero-extended load_data as part of a forwarding value: select load_data for mem_to_reg, otherwise the existing EX/MEM alu_result. implementation_notes:
# MEM-to-EX load forwarding

Implemented the hypothesis in cores/bench only. mem_stage exposes fwd_data,
selecting its existing sign/zero-extended load_data for mem_to_reg and the
registered ALU result otherwise. fwd_w_en uses in.valid and the alignment-trap
corrected ctrl_with_trap.reg_write. core connects those outputs to the existing
highest-priority EX/MEM forwarding path. forward_unit retains its nonzero
destination check, simultaneous rs1/rs2 matching and younger-MEM-over-WB priority.
Misaligned loads cannot produce a forwarding value or write a register.

Removed the unconditional load-use bubble and the now-unused hazard-unit source
index/destination inputs. All other hazard controls remain: dmem stalls hold PC,
ID/EX and EX/MEM, clear only MEM/WB.valid, and retain WB forwarding provenance.
Ready qualification happens at consumption: EX cannot advance, redirect or launch
the divider while the older memory operation is unaccepted. The MEM forwarding
producer remains selected during a hold, preserving younger-writer priority.
The existing formatted load result is captured by the consumer on the same edge
that accepts the load. No stage, queue, speculative state or additional latency
was introduced. Divider RTL, seven-clock real/ALTOPS execution, operand capture,
held DONE, decoder legality, retirement order and nret=1 IO are unchanged.

Expanded pipeline tests cover every legal byte/halfword offset, signed and
unsigned loads, positive/negative/zero/all-one values, both matching operands,
ALU/multiply, load/store addresses, store data, branch/JALR and all four divide
operations. They check exact retirement PCs, source values, results, raw memory
words/masks, accepted reads/writes and order. Tests require adjacent zero-wait
load/ordinary-consumer retirements and a nine-clock load/divide retirement gap.
They also cover conservative source-index matches, x0, younger loads overriding
held WB, older WB needed by a stalled consumer, misaligned loads, long/random
stalls with changing unaccepted dmem data, and redirects during imem stalls.
The existing ten-cycle zero-wait liveness bound remains enforced. EX divider
tests change the MEM forwarding input before acceptance and all inputs after
launch, check exact seven-clock completion, held DONE, captured RVFI operands
and single publication for DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU.

Local validation of the final design:

- Required Verilator lint command: pass, no warnings.
- RTL_DIR=cores/bench/rtl CORE_NAME=bench JOBS=8 bash formal/run_all.sh:
  pass, 53 checks passed and 0 failed, including liveness. No formal failures,
  counterexamples or corrective retries were needed.
- make test TARGET=bench: all 8 pytest runners passed, including real/ALTOPS
  divider arithmetic and the expanded pipeline/EX tests.
- NRET=1 make cosim TARGET=bench: pass, 5 ELFs tested. Selftest and the three
  existing random programs were compared to the ISS with and without bus stalls;
  CoreMark passed canonical CRC/UART/OOB checks with benchmark stalls.
- make timing TARGET=bench: placement option 0 Fmax 47.215 MHz.
- NRET=1 make fpga TARGET=bench: placements 47.215/47.350/47.350 MHz;
  median 47.350 MHz, 2,849 logic cells, 643 registers. Marker-bracketed CoreMark
  took 4,287,652 cycles for 10 iterations. Fitness: 110.43 iterations/second.

The direct make cosim build defaults to NRET=2, so its first invocation failed
to compile the absent channel-1 ports. Supplying NRET=1 matches core.yaml; no
evaluation or formal configuration files were modified.

Concern: the throughput improvement does not clear the stated 4.6% acceptance
threshold. Relative to 4,491,485 champion cycles, cycles fell 4.54% and iterations
per cycle rose 4.75%, but median Fmax fell from 48.625 to 47.350 MHz. Fitness rose
only 2.00%, from 108.26 to 110.43 (threshold approximately 113.24). The worst vendor
path traverses dmem BRAM, MEM load formatting, EX forwarding, the multiplier and
EX output selection back to a dmem address, with 15 logic cells. This timing
penalty is measured, not inferred from IPC alone.

Two local combinational timing experiments were evaluated and reverted: merging
EX forwarding/ALU input muxes into parallel masked selects scored 102.49, and
parallel MEM load formatting scored 109.15. Both passed formal, but neither
improved the direct bypass. The final RTL restores the original formatting and
EX mux logic and was rechecked with formal, cosim and all-placement FPGA fitness.

title: Separate live load forwarding from registered multiplier operands
motivation:
The champion scores 108.26 iterations/second with median Gowin Fmax
48.625 MHz and 4,491,485 bracketed CoreMark cycles. LESSONS.md is absent.
The two prior structural attempts removed and folded combinational
division; the latest notes identify forwarding/control as a competing
limit. A fresh vendor timing run reproduced the champion and found
branch flush feedback, operand selection into multiplication, and the
five-step divider at nearly equal delays.
An isolated validity-only control prototype reached 49.533 MHz,
insufficient by itself. A full MEM-to-EX load bypass reduced bracketed
cycles to 4,287,652 with canonical CRCs, but fell to 43.755 MHz because
loaded data could pass through the multiplier into the next address.
This supports a selective forwarding topology that saves load-use
bubbles while physically excluding live memory data from multiplication.

title: Direction-only prediction with one-bit branch recovery
motivation:
No LESSONS.md is present. The two prior predictor attempts passed formal
and cosim and reduced the roughly 4.49M CoreMark cycles to 4.20M. The
fetch-time bimodal attempt ran on the old combinational-divider parent;
its 5.292 MHz result does not measure predictor timing on this champion.
The later tagged target predictor used 96 LUTRAMs and 4475 LUT4s, reached
31.556 MHz on its slower-divider parent, and saved almost no additional
cycles over direction prediction. Neither became champion. The current
five-step-divider champion reaches 48.625 MHz and fitness 108.26, with a
worst path through ID, EX, IF and hazard logic. Predictor recovery delay
therefore matters now. Removing correctly predicted direct-transfer
bubbles while comparing only branch direction offers the previous cycle
savings without a target table or a wide actual-versus-predicted-PC test.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one compact direct-control-flow predictor to the existing pipeline:
a 64-entry two-bit bimodal conditional-branch direction table indexed by
fetch PC[7:2], plus unconditional prediction of aligned legal JAL. Reset
counters to weakly taken (10). Lookup depends only on the registered PC
and old counter state; there is no EX-to-fetch training bypass. Predecode
legal BRANCH funct3 values and JAL from raw imem_data, form their exact
sign-extended B/J targets with PC plus immediate, and predict taken only
if that target is word aligned. Everything else, including JALR and
reserved branch encodings, predicts sequential PC+4. No target/tag array,
return stack, global history, instruction buffer or new pipeline stage
is part of this hypothesis.

Carry only a predicted_taken bit with each accepted fetched instruction
into ID/EX. Since direct targets are computed from that same instruction
and PC in both fetch and EX, direction is sufficient to establish a
correct direct prediction; do not add a 32-bit predicted_next_pc field
or compare two complete next-PC values. In EX, define effective taken
as a legal taken branch or legal jump with no target-alignment trap.
Recover a conditional branch exactly when effective taken XOR its
captured predicted_taken bit is one. Aligned JAL is already predicted
exactly and needs no recovery; JALR retains its existing EX redirect.
Non-control instructions cannot create predictions because lookup is
qualified by the current fetched instruction, not a stale PC tag.
Misaligned direct targets are never predicted, and EX retains the
existing trap, link-write suppression and sequential successor behavior.

Preselect the conditional recovery address using the registered prediction
bit: predicted taken means recovery to the branch's own PC+4; predicted
not taken means recovery to its direct branch target. Do not use the late
operand comparison to choose this recovery address, and do not feed the
architectural next-PC mux into mismatch detection. Thus the flush/PC
enable decision adds only a one-bit mismatch test to branch resolution.
RVFI pc_wdata continues to use the actual architectural next PC, and
JAL/JALR link values remain PC+4. Correct predictions admit the fetched
successor into ID/EX as the predecessor advances, with no flush bubble.

Implement recovery as a validity/ID-register flush, not as a 32-bit
fetched-instruction rewrite. Remove redirect from IF's instruction-data
NOP mux: flush_if may still insert the current imem-stall NOP, while
redirect independently invalidates fetch and asserts the existing
accepting ID/EX flush. Predecode always observes raw imem_data. This
keeps late recovery out of instruction decode and source-address
comparison. A recovery-capable EX branch/jump is not a load, and recovery
already overrides PC holding; wrong-path instruction bits cannot create
a retirement or memory side effect. Keep every downstream valid gate
and pipeline flush intact, including rejection of a wrong-path divide.

Train one counter exactly once when a valid, legal, nontrapping conditional
branch transfers from EX to EX/MEM. Saturate toward the actual branch
outcome; do not update for holds, divider waits, bubbles or jumps. A
simultaneous fetch/update at the same index sees the old counter, and
the instruction captures the decision actually used to advance its PC.
Use the existing EX acceptance gate (!stall_ex_mem, !reset, no active
divide) for recovery and training. Fetch prediction changes PC only when
the corresponding valid instruction is accepted into ID/EX. Preserve
predicted_taken on ID/EX holds and clear it on reset or bubbles. Reset
overrides recovery; accepted EX recovery overrides imem backpressure;
otherwise load-use, imem, dmem and divider stalls hold fetch as today.
Never recover or train a branch while an older stalled MEM operation
prevents its transfer. Preserve held-WB forwarding and all memory gates.

Keep the champion's divider, ALU, register file, retirement width and
stage topology unchanged. The earlier approximately 6.9% throughput
gain from direct prediction motivates an expected 8% fitness improvement
if compact recovery maintains or slightly improves Fmax. This is a
measured hypothesis, not a guaranteed gain: fetch target addition and
BHT lookup may become timing limits. Judge it by median Gowin Fmax times
marker-bracketed CoreMark iterations/cycle; it must exceed fitness 113.24
to clear the 4.6% acceptance margin and pass all unchanged correctness
checks, canonical CRCs and UART validation.

implementation_notes:
Implemented direction-only prediction in cores/bench.

- IF predecodes raw instruction data for legal BRANCH funct3 values and
  JAL, computes exact signed B/J targets, and predicts only aligned
  targets. The 64-entry two-bit table uses PC[7:2], resets to 10, and has
  no training bypass. JALR, reserved branch encodings, and other opcodes
  remain sequential at fetch.
- IF/ID and ID/EX carry one predicted_taken bit. ID captures it with the
  instruction, retains it on holds, and clears it on reset/bubbles.
- Accepted EX conditional branches recover on effective direction XOR
  captured prediction. Their recovery address is selected by the
  registered prediction: PC+4 for predicted taken, direct target for
  predicted not taken. Correct JAL predictions do not redirect; aligned
  JALR retains EX redirect. Architectural RVFI pc_next, links, alignment
  traps, and link-write suppression retain their original behavior.
- Recovery invalidates fetch and flushes ID/EX. Redirect no longer
  rewrites fetched instruction bits or drives hazard_unit.flush_if;
  imem backpressure still inserts the existing NOP. Reset wins over
  recovery, accepted recovery wins over imem holds, and older stalled
  MEM operations prevent both recovery and training.
- Exactly one accepted, legal, nontrapping conditional branch updates
  its counter. Existing memory gates, held-WB forwarding, divider, ALU,
  register file, retirement width, and pipeline stages are unchanged.

Implementation detail versus the advisory plan: each counter has local
decoded write enable and Boolean saturating next-state equations. This
removes the indexed training-read mux while preserving the specified
64x2 table and old-state lookup behavior. Training exports the six PC
index bits rather than an unused complete PC. No architectural deviation.

Tests added/updated:
- Pipeline tests independently model every fetched prediction, accepted
  recovery, prediction capture/hold/bubble, and accepted training event.
  They compare training events with retired nontrapping branches and
  check complete RVFI PC/order/source/result/link and memory behavior.
- Directed programs cover loop warmup and exit, both mismatch directions,
  saturation, PC-index aliases, negative B/J targets, back-to-back direct
  transfers, reset after training, reserved branch funct3, misaligned
  BRANCH/JAL/JALR, load/divide dependencies, held-WB forwarding, wrong-path
  divides/stores, and directed plus seeded random imem/dmem stalls.
- Fetch unit tests cover saturation boundaries, synchronous reset,
  simultaneous lookup/update using old state, absence of training bypass,
  raw predecode, alignment, and reset/recovery/backpressure priority.
- Direct-transfer-to-divide schedule now requires nine cycles for correct
  BRANCH/JAL predictions and ten for unresolved JALR. Existing arithmetic,
  operand, PC, wrong-path-store, and randomized-stall checks remain.
- Standalone EX divider test bundle packing includes the new bit.

Local validation:
- Required Verilator -Wall lint: PASS, no warnings.
- Complete cocotb pytest suite: 9 runners passed. After the local-counter
  RTL refinement, fetch/pipeline predictor runners passed again.
- Unchanged formal/run_all.sh, RTL_DIR=cores/bench/rtl CORE_NAME=bench:
  PASS, 53 passed / 0 failed, both initial and final RTL. No formal
  failures, counterexamples, or repair attempts.
- Unchanged cosim: selftest plus three random trace programs checked
  against the ISS, with and without random bus stalls, and CoreMark
  CRC/UART validation. PASS for all five ELFs. Use NRET=1 when invoking
  make cosim/make fpga locally because build.sh otherwise defaults to 2;
  core.yaml and top-level ports remain nret=1.
- Canonical CoreMark validates seedcrc=e9f5, crclist=e714, crcmatrix=1fd7,
  crcstate=8e3a, crcfinal=fcaf and "Correct operation validated." with
  the unchanged 2K, -O3, ITERATIONS=10 benchmark and random bus stalls.

Measured final Gowin/fitness result (NRET=1 make fpga TARGET=bench):
- Placement Fmax: option 0 = 48.264 MHz; options 1 and 2 = 47.603 MHz.
- Median Fmax = 47.603 MHz.
- Marker-bracketed CoreMark cycles = 4,201,709, iterations = 10.
- Fitness = 113.29 iterations/second, versus champion 108.26 (+4.65%).
- Area: 3123 LUT4/logic, 772 FF, 8 LUTRAM, 6 BSRAM, 6 DSP.

Concern: fitness clears the required 113.24 margin by only 0.05. The
cycle savings are present, but median Fmax is below the champion's
48.625 MHz. Final acceptance still depends on the orchestrator's unchanged
correctness and vendor timing gates. The first indexed-update table
implementation measured 47.199 MHz / fitness 112.33; local counter updates
improved that result without changing instruction timing or prediction.

title: Shorten five-bit divider groups with mixed-radix parallel trials
motivation:
The current champion scores 113.92 at 48.843 MHz, and its reported worst
path runs from quotient_q to remainder_q inside div_unit: 25.763 ns and
162 cells. Each normal RUN clock cascades five full-width restoring
subtract-and-select steps. The earlier micro_opt radix-4 attempt
hyp-20261004-001-r2s0 increased Fmax from its 32.136 MHz parent to
42.346 MHz, but did not beat the competing five-bit scheduling change.
It used four radix-4 steps per clock, unlike the shorter mixed-radix
group proposed here. The current seven-clock schedule and isolated
multiplier operands provide a better parent for optimizing just the
divider recurrence, without adding CoreMark cycles or another bypass.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Rewrite only the real arithmetic inside div_unit while retaining its
launch, six five-bit RUN groups, final two-bit RUN group with fused
sign restoration, and held DONE/consume behavior. Replace each normal
five-bit group with two radix-4 restoring digit steps followed by one
radix-2 restoring bit step. This consumes exactly five dividend bits
and produces exactly five quotient bits, but reduces serial full-width
arithmetic stages from five to three. Use the first radix-4 step alone
for the final group, since exactly two dividend bits remain after the
six normal groups. Keep seven RUN clocks in real and ALTOPS builds;
this is a combinational datapath optimization within the existing
registers, not a change in pipeline topology or instruction latency.

At accepted launch, capture unsigned divisor magnitude D and its
widened multiples 2D and 3D. Use explicitly sized 34-bit values;
form 3D from zero-extended D plus 2D at launch and register it, so
RUN never includes multiple generation. Each radix-4 step forms the
34-bit trial T = {remainder[31:0], quotient[31:30]} and computes T-D,
T-2D, and T-3D in parallel using 35-bit zero-extended subtractions.
Bit 34 is the borrow indicator for these unsigned bounded operands.
Let ok1, ok2, ok3 mean no borrow for those three differences. Append
quotient digit {ok2, ok3 | (ok1 & !ok2)}. Select the low 32 remainder
bits with disjoint masks !ok1, ok1 & !ok2, ok2 & !ok3, and ok3 on T
and the corresponding differences. Express the selection as parallel
masked OR rather than cascading priority muxes. Feed the selected
remainder and shifted quotient into the next digit step. The third,
radix-2 step uses the existing shared subtraction/borrow recurrence.

For nonzero D, each restored remainder is less than D, so the
registered and inter-step restored remainder still needs only 32
bits. For D=0, all trials succeed: radix-4 emits 11 and radix-2 emits
1, producing quotient 0xffffffff and the dividend magnitude as
remainder after all 32 bits. Preserve the existing rule suppressing
quotient negation for zero divisors, and restore remainder sign only
from the dividend. Preserve DIV(INT_MIN,-1)=INT_MIN and
REM(INT_MIN,-1)=0, including all unsigned values with bit 31 set.
The final group must sign-correct the first radix-4 step's completed
quotient and remainder, rather than the five-bit normal-group result.

Leave EX integration, operand capture, forwarding, stall arbitration,
decoder legality, retirement ordering, nret=1 ports, and all formal
formulas unchanged. Keep result_valid asserted until consume and
reset behavior identical. Existing unit tests must retain their exact
seven-clock completion and held-result assertions in both arithmetic
modes. Add directed and independent randomized checks of the real
mixed-radix recurrence, including maximum-width multiples, all radix-4
digits, five-bit group boundaries, and final-group sign correction.
Run unchanged formal, cocotb, cosim, and canonical CoreMark gates.

The predicted fitness gain comes from higher Gowin Fmax at the same
instruction latency. Additional parallel subtractors and the launch
path through signed magnitude plus 3D generation are the main timing
risks; the integer/load and multiplier paths can also become the new
limit. Judge the result by median vendor Fmax times marker-bracketed
iterations/cycle under the existing bus stalls. With unchanged cycles,
Fmax must exceed about 51.09 MHz, and fitness must exceed 119.16, to
clear the champion's 4.6 percent acceptance margin.

motivation:
The champion scores 113.92 at 48.843 MHz. Its worst Gowin path is now

Restructure only the shared multicycle divider into one preparation
clock, five clocks that each process three radix-4 digits (six dividend
bits), and one terminal clock that processes a single radix-4 digit
(two bits) and restores the result sign. This consumes exactly 32 bits
in seven RUN clocks, preserving the existing completion schedule and
all pipeline boundaries. The recurring datapath has three dependent
subtract/select stages instead of five; the terminal path has one
digit stage followed by sign restoration.

At the accepted launch edge L, capture the dividend magnitude, divisor
magnitude D, operation and sign flags exactly as today. Do not compute
3D on the launch path: it already includes forwarding and potentially
live load data. At edge L+1, use the captured D to register the unsigned
34-bit value 3D = zero_extend(D) + (zero_extend(D) << 1), while retaining
quotient and remainder unchanged. D and 2D are explicitly widened to
34 bits from the captured divisor; 2D is a wiring shift. All RUN digit
arithmetic uses these registered sources, never live operands.

Reuse one physical chain of three radix-4 digit cells on edges L+2
through L+6. Each cell forms the 34-bit unsigned trial
T = {remainder[31:0], quotient[31:30]} and computes T-D, T-2D and T-3D
in parallel as explicitly zero-extended 35-bit subtractions. Bit 34
indicates borrow; do not implement a comparison followed by a second
subtraction. Let ok1, ok2 and ok3 be the three no-borrow predicates.
Append quotient digit {ok2, ok3 | (ok1 & !ok2)}. Select the low 32 bits
of the next remainder using disjoint masks !ok1, ok1 & !ok2,
ok2 & !ok3 and ok3 on T and the respective differences, expressed as
a parallel masked OR rather than cascaded priority muxes. Shift the
quotient by two per cell and register the third cell's outputs after
each full group. For nonzero D the restored remainder is below D,
so 32-bit remainder storage is sufficient even for large divisors.

select the requested operation and register result while entering DONE.

digits. Keep result_valid low through L+6 and assert it immediately
after L+7. The existing three-bit group counter can encode preparation

unchanged captured subtraction/XOR formulas; no faster formal-only

title: Folded-PC bimodal prediction with one-bit recovery
motivation:
No LESSONS.md exists. The earlier 64-entry PC[7:2] bimodal direction
predictor passed formal and cosim and used 4,201,709 CoreMark cycles,
versus its parent's 4,491,485, but median Fmax fell to 47.603 MHz and
fitness 113.29 lost to the concurrently improved core. The current
champion keeps integer load forwarding separate from multiplier operands
and reaches fitness 113.92 at 48.843 MHz with 4,287,652 cycles. The tagged
target predictor saved only about 4,200 additional cycles over direct
direction prediction while consuming 96 LUTRAMs, so it is unattractive.

A local experiment built the unchanged canonical 2K, -O3, ten-iteration
CoreMark ELF and recorded its architectural trace with the existing ISS.
A cycle replay using the contract's xorshift bus-ready draws, selective
load-to-MUL interlock and divider latency exactly reproduced both parent
cycle counts above and the earlier predictor's 4,201,709-cycle result.
On the current parent it predicts 3,997,209 cycles for the old bimodal
index, versus 3,985,515 for the same 64x2 table indexed by
PC[7:2] XOR PC[13:8]. Conditional misses fall from 51,854 to 41,562.
A 256-entry, six-bit-history gshare model instead needs 4,005,636 cycles;
history adds cost without a measured accuracy advantage here. Folding
two adjacent PC slices reduces harmful aliases without adding counters,
tags or speculative state.

title: Speculative non-restoring pairs with parallel signed divisor preparation
motivation:
No LESSONS.md exists. The champion scores 126.34 iter/sec at 50.352 MHz
with 3,985,515 marker-bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its 25.608 ns worst
path crosses 164 cells inside the five-step restoring divider.
Prior mixed-radix and retimed radix-4 attempts reached 51.856 and
52.657 MHz on the preceding parent but moved the limit into integer
forwarding. A local speculative non-restoring pair prototype on this
champion passed both real and ALTOPS divider tests and reached median
51.889 MHz. Its divisor preparation still serializes magnitude, triple
generation and triple negation. Prepare signed triples directly from
the raw divisor to remove one full-width arithmetic dependency and
make the pair recurrence the single proposed micro-optimization.
The refined scratch prototype measured 50.440/54.419/54.419 MHz across
the evaluator's three Gowin placement options, median 54.419 MHz,
with 3,816 LUT4s and 869 registers. Both real and ALTOPS divider suites
passed. This is an 8.08 percent Fmax gain with unchanged execution
latency; full scored CoreMark and formal acceptance remain evaluator
gates, so the prototype timing is not a claim of measured fitness.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace only div_unit's real restoring arithmetic with signed partial
remainders and speculative pairs of non-restoring radix-2 steps.
Preserve six five-bit groups, the final two-bit group, seven RUN clocks,
all launch/consume semantics and the existing CPU pipeline. Each normal
group uses two speculative two-bit cells followed by one ordinary
non-restoring bit cell; the terminal group uses the first pair alone.
This changes local combinational arithmetic and a few divider registers,
without changing any instruction's latency or stall behavior.

Capture unsigned divisor magnitude D and a 33-bit two's-complement
-D at launch. Use a signed 33-bit partial remainder R initialized to
zero, so all unsigned divisors through 0xffffffff are representable.
One non-restoring step with dividend bit b computes
R1=2R+b+(R<0 ? D : -D), and emits quotient bit !(R1<0).
Keep the recurrence in explicitly sized 33-bit modular arithmetic.
For D nonzero its selected result stays in [-D,D), so bit 32 is the
correct sign even when an intermediate shifted value wraps.

For a pair with incoming bits b1,b0 let S=4R+2*b1+b0 modulo 2^33.
In parallel compute the ordinary first-step R1 and both possible
second-step results:
  N = S + (R<0 ? 3D : -D);
  P = S + (R<0 ? D : -3D).
Select R2 = R1<0 ? N : P and append the two quotient bits
{!(R1<0),!(R2<0)}. Derive both N and P directly from incoming R and
the two dividend bits, not by doubling the just-computed R1.
The first-step sign and two second-step candidates therefore traverse
parallel carry chains. A pair has one dependent arithmetic depth plus
selection, rather than two serial arithmetic depths. Use precomputed
+/-D and +/-3D registers and two candidate adders per pair; avoid
expanding into four complete second-step adders, which increases
routing without an observed timing advantage.

Prepare +/-3D directly from the forwarded raw divisor b in parallel
with magnitude capture. Define s=signed_op&&b[31], B={s,b}, and
H=B+(B<<1), explicitly 33 bits throughout. Compute J=33'd0-H once.
Register +3D as s ? J : H and -3D as s ? H : J. This eliminates the
slower sequence abs(b), then 3*abs(b), then its negation. These are
residues modulo 2^33, not truncated positive mathematical multiples;
their use in the pair sums is exact because selected R2 fits signed
33 bits. Similarly capture -D directly as s ? {1'b1,b} :
(33'd0-{1'b0,b}), so divisor negation never follows magnitude negation.
Select the signed operation and remainder/quotient sign flags exactly
as in the current divider.

After the terminal pair, correct a negative partial remainder by
adding D; otherwise use its low 32 bits. Restore the requested signed
quotient and remainder signs in parallel from the terminal quotient
and this corrected remainder, then capture result on the existing
group_q==6 edge. Keep sign correction connected to the first pair,
never the normal five-bit group's result, so terminal timing cannot
include unused later pair/bit cells. For D=0 the recurrence emits all
quotient ones and retains the dividend magnitude; keep existing
suppression of quotient sign negation for zero divisors. Preserve
remainder sign from the dividend, DIV(INT_MIN,-1)=INT_MIN and
REM(INT_MIN,-1)=0.

title: Two-entry fall-through fetch queue overlaps instruction stalls with backend holds
motivation:
The champion achieves 126.34 iterations/second at 50.352 MHz and
3,985,515 marker-bracketed CoreMark cycles. No LESSONS.md exists.
Structural history already covers multicycle division, shorter divider
groups, multiplier operand isolation, and radix-4 divider retiming.
The latest divider retiming reached 52.657 MHz but exposed a competing
register-file/EX path; further arithmetic shortening has limited margin.
The current front end has no instruction storage: dmem stalls, division
waits, and load-to-MUL interlocks all freeze the fetch PC. Available
instruction-bus cycles during these backend holds are discarded, and
later independent instruction-bus stalls still create decode bubbles.
A small elastic queue can improve iterations/cycle while preserving
the existing arithmetic and single-retirement execution pipeline.

hypothesis.hypothesis:

registered instruction entries and an empty-queue combinational bypass.
Each entry carries PC, raw instruction, and the direction prediction
made when that instruction is fetched. Retain the champion's folded-PC

instruction pipeline, memory organization, arithmetic, predictor table

The training register accepts at most one event each clock, matching
nret=1 and the existing single EX acceptance boundary. The previous
registered event updates its counter on that same edge, so back-to-back
accepted branches sustain one update per clock without a queue or loss.
Capture only the event's index and outcome, never a snapshot of counter
state: apply each event to the current counter state in original branch
acceptance order. Consecutive same-index events must therefore compose
correctly even when their outcomes alternate or a counter saturates.

Use exactly the current PC[7:2] XOR PC[13:8] index and weakly taken (10)
counter reset state. Table lookup reads old registered counter MSBs.
Do not bypass either the current EX outcome or the pending registered
update into fetch. A branch may consequently make a guess from one

bit with its accepted instruction, as today, so recovery remains exact.

train_valid already qualifies an accepted legal nontrapping EX branch.

title: Borrow-lookahead carry-select subtraction in the restoring divider
motivation:
The current champion scores 134.59 iter/sec at 51.54 MHz, with
3,829,487 marker-bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its reported worst Gowin
path goes from remainder_q back to remainder_q inside div_unit,
crossing 152 cells with a 24.838 ns arrival time. Each ordinary RUN
clock cascades five 33-bit subtract-and-restore cells. No LESSONS.md
exists. Prior micro_opt attempts used radix-4 trials, mixed-radix
groups, or speculative non-restoring pairs; these either increased
arithmetic area or moved the limit to integer forwarding, and the
latest non-restoring attempt regressed. Target the carry propagation
inside the existing radix-2 cells instead of changing the recurrence.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the monolithic subtraction in each of div_unit's five
restoring bit cells with an explicitly segmented borrow-lookahead,
carry-select subtractor. Keep the unsigned restoring recurrence,
operand registers, six five-bit groups, terminal two-bit group,
fused sign restoration, and exactly seven RUN clocks unchanged.
This is one combinational arithmetic optimization; no CPU stage,
predictor, forwarding path, instruction latency or memory policy
changes are included.

In each bit cell form X={R[31:0],Q[31]} and subtract {1'b0,D}.
Partition X[31:0] and D into four eight-bit blocks, numbered from
least significant to most significant. For block k compute in
parallel a nine-bit local subtraction t0[k]={1'b0,X_k}-{1'b0,D_k},
its generate bit g[k]=t0[k][8], and propagate p[k]=(X_k==D_k).
Set incoming borrow b[0]=0 and form b[1] through b[4] with explicit
balanced prefix generate/propagate equations, not a dependent chain
of four general-purpose arithmetic operators. The final low-word
borrow is b[4]. Because the subtrahend's bit 32 is zero, the true
33-bit borrow is !X[32] && b[4]; this formula must also handle X[32]=1.
Do not infer a signed comparison or silently drop X[32].

For upper blocks compute the eight-bit alternative difference
t1[k]=X_k+(~D_k), modulo 256, alongside t0[k]. This is subtraction
with an incoming borrow of one. Select each block's low difference
from t0[k][7:0] or t1[k] using its prefix-derived b[k]; block zero
needs only t0[0]. Build the accepted low 32-bit difference from
those four selected blocks. Restore R_next to X[31:0] on true
borrow, otherwise use that low difference; append !borrow to the
quotient. Expose independent per-block signals or an acyclic helper
module so synthesis can retain short native carry chains and parallel
prefix logic. No full-width subtraction may remain in a restoring
cell, and do not serialize t1 after t0 with an increment/decrement.

Preserve the existing signed-magnitude launch and terminal sign
correction. The last RUN edge must still consume quotient_step[2]
and remainder_step[2], never the unused normal five-step output.
Preserve all exact RV32M cases: zero divisor produces quotient all
ones and the original dividend remainder, zero-divisor quotient
negation remains suppressed, signed remainder follows only the
dividend, and INT_MIN/-1 yields INT_MIN quotient and zero remainder.
Keep the ALTOPS formulas and identical seven-clock completion schedule.
Keep reset cancellation, rejected starts, simultaneous consume/start,
stable DONE retention, EX operand/RVFI capture, nret=1 ports, decoder
legality, retirement order, liveness, and all bus-stall behavior.

The intended gain is shorter borrow and difference propagation in
every dependent restoring step at unchanged CoreMark cycles. The
main risks are duplicated block arithmetic, prefix routing and the
existing integer/forwarding paths becoming the clock limit. The
estimate is not a measured fitness result. Require unchanged formal,
arithmetic unit, stalled cosim, memory-bound, CRC and UART gates,
with canonical marker-bracketed cycles. At unchanged cycles the
acceptance threshold is median Gowin Fmax greater than 53.91084 MHz,
or fitness greater than 140.78114 iter/sec; small placement variation
alone does not establish the hypothesis.

title: Dedicated leading-byte divider stage enables a four-bit shared body
motivation:
LESSONS.md is absent. The champion reaches 134.59 iter/sec at 51.540 MHz
with 3,829,487 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its worst reported path is the
five-step restoring divider, at 24.838 ns and 152 cells. Prior radix-4
retiming reached 52.657 MHz but still used three full-width digit cells.
Fully spatial scratch probes passed real and ALTOPS arithmetic/handshake
tests, but duplicated stage registers increased routing and reduced
option-0 Fmax to 34.899/46.641 MHz. The promising structural alternative

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the uniform seven-group divider with one dedicated leading-eight-
bit stage followed by six four-bit RUN groups using one shared two-digit
radix-4 body. Launch edge L captures magnitudes and signs as today.
At L+1 compute the first eight quotient bits and partial remainder from
the dividend's leading byte, and prepare registered full-width 3D in
parallel. At L+2 through L+7 consume four bits per clock. The final group
fuses sign restoration and result selection before entering DONE.
Exactly 8+6*4=32 dividend bits are processed in seven RUN clocks.
This is one structural stage specialization and folding change; keep
instruction latency, CPU pipeline stages and retirement width unchanged.

Implement the leading-byte stage as two narrow radix-16 trial cells.
For each four-bit digit, compare its trial T in parallel against j*D
for j=1..15, select the largest successful j, subtract that multiple,
and append the four-bit quotient digit. The first trial contains only
the leading nibble; the second combines the first selected remainder
and next nibble. Because the complete prefix is at most 255, any set
divisor bit in [31:8] rejects every nonzero digit and leaves the prefix
unchanged. Otherwise use D[7:0]. Share explicitly sized 12-bit constant
shift/add multiples j*D[7:0] between both cells, with 13-bit zero-extended
subtractions for combined borrow detection and remainder candidates.
Never truncate the multiples to eight bits before comparison.

Include digit zero as always eligible. Monotonic success bits give
select[j]=ok[j]&&!ok[j+1], with select[15]=ok[15]. Select the remainder
and digit using disjoint masked ORs, avoiding a serial priority cascade.
The first cell's remainder fits four bits, and the completed prefix
remainder fits eight. Store the prefix quotient by shifting the original
quotient/dividend register eight bits and appending the computed byte.

Register unsigned 34-bit 3D on L+1 from the already captured divisor
magnitude, independently of the prefix arithmetic. Do not generate 3D
on the live forwarded launch path. Widen D and 2D to 34 bits, with 2D a
wiring shift. The reusable body has exactly two dependent radix-4 cells.
Each forms 34-bit T={R,Q[31:30]}, computes T-D, T-2D and T-3D as parallel
35-bit unsigned subtractions, and derives success from clear borrow.
Append digit {ok2,ok3|(ok1&!ok2)}. Select the low 32-bit remainder with
disjoint masks !ok1, ok1&!ok2, ok2&!ok3 and ok3 on T and the differences.
Register the second cell's quotient and remainder after normal groups.
On group six restore both signs in parallel from that cell's completed
outputs, select quotient versus remainder, register result and enter
DONE. Never use stale state, padding steps, or the old two-bit terminal.

Retain shared quotient/remainder/divisor registers plus a divisor triple;
do not duplicate the entire divider into spatial stages. Group zero
uses the prefix stage, while groups one through six use the body only
after prefix and triple registers are ready. Use scalar or generate-local
signals to expose acyclic cell dependencies to lint. Preserve reset
cancellation, start/busy/result_valid/consume ports, rejected starts,
simultaneous consume/relaunch and stable DONE retention.

For D=0 every prefix digit is 15 and every body digit is 3, yielding
quotient 0xffffffff and original-dividend magnitude as remainder.
Retain zero-divisor suppression of quotient negation, dividend-only
remainder sign, DIV(INT_MIN,-1)=INT_MIN and REM(INT_MIN,-1)=0.
Keep exact ALTOPS subtraction/XOR formulas and identical seven-RUN
completion timing in real and formal builds. Preserve EX forwarded
operand/RVFI capture, single publication, pipeline draining and dmem
holds, nine-cycle consecutive-divide and ten-cycle redirect-to-divide
retirement gaps, nret=1 ports, strict RVFI order, decoder legality,
multiplier isolation, fetch queue, predictor and all correctness gates.

Expect eight percent fitness improvement at unchanged CoreMark cycles.
Confidence is medium pending vendor timing: prefix selection, the final
four-bit/sign path, or existing integer/multiplier paths may cap Fmax.
Spatial probe timings are evidence against full duplication, not
measurements of the final asymmetric circuit. Require fitness above
140.78114 iter/sec; unchanged-cycle median Gowin Fmax must exceed
53.91084 MHz. Preserve canonical CRCs, UART validation, bounded accesses
and MMIO timing brackets, and evaluate the final median vendor timing.

immediately fetching through the registered target avoids an added
misprediction bubble and preserves the tight divider liveness window.

implementation_notes:
# One-bit registered predictor squash

Implemented the proposed control split. Correctness gates pass, but the
measured implementation does not meet the fitness acceptance threshold.

## RTL changes

- `cores/bench/rtl/ex_stage.sv`: retained the existing accepted immediate
  redirect and preselected target. Added exactly one registered squash bit,
  assigned from that accepted redirect each edge and cleared on reset and
  every following no-event edge. Squash excludes the younger EX instruction
  from recovery, predictor training, divider launch/wait and next EX/MEM
  validity. Its ordinary wide payload still captures through the existing
  pipeline path, including ordinary trap adjustments.
- `cores/bench/rtl/if_stage.sv`: immediate redirect controls only the ordinary
  full 32-bit PC register. Reset wins, then redirect, then accepted fetch.
  The registered squash bypasses obsolete queue entries with the word at the
  corrected PC. An available consumed target leaves zero occupancy; an
  available unconsumed target becomes the sole head; an unavailable target
  clears occupancy and retries the same PC. PC advances exactly once per
  accepted target fetch. `imem_addr` remains directly assigned from PC.
- `cores/bench/rtl/hazard_unit.sv`: replaced immediate redirect arbitration
  with squash qualification. Fresh target decode ignores the killed younger
  load-to-MUL interlock and divider wait while retaining older-memory holds
  and the ordinary load-to-MUL bubble.
- `cores/bench/rtl/core.sv`: wired immediate redirect/target to IF PC recovery
  and the registered event to IF queue handling and hazard arbitration.
  Retirement, forwarding provenance and top-level ports were preserved.

The 64x2 folded-PC bimodal table, weakly-taken reset, Boolean saturation,
aligned legal BRANCH/JAL predecode and EX training boundary are unchanged.
There is no extra target register, fetch-address mux, training pipeline,
target table, history, return stack, arithmetic change or retirement stage.

## Tests and deviations

Updated the independent queue and pipeline models for the delayed occupancy
discard while preserving immediate PC correction. Added exhaustive recovery
occupancy/ready/accept checks, high-address preservation, retry/reset checks,
target BRANCH/JAL prediction and same-edge old-state prediction capture.

Added directed pipeline cases for both conditional mismatch directions and
JALR, including younger stores, aligned/misaligned loads, MUL, DIV, branches,
misaligned branches and JALR. Checks verify target acceptance timing, actual
RVFI operands/targets/links/order, unchanged ten-cycle recovery-to-DIV gaps,
memory request provenance, training suppression and ordinary invalid payload
capture under independent bus stalls. Existing assertions remain intact;
the harness additionally compares accepted load requests with the ISA model.

The only addition beyond the advisory test files is
`cores/bench/test/test_ex_divider.py`, which directly checks accepted-event
qualification, one-cycle pulse clearing, validity-only EX/MEM killing,
divider suppression and reset of a pending event.

## Local validation

- Required Verilator lint command: PASS, no warnings.
- `RTL_DIR=cores/bench/rtl CORE_NAME=bench JOBS=8 bash formal/run_all.sh`:
  PASS on the first run, 53 passed / 0 failed, including liveness, unique,
  register provenance and all instruction checks. No formal counterexample
  and no formal fix/retry attempts were needed. This is the standard ALTOPS
  gate; arithmetic RTL was unchanged.
- Cocotb: all 10 pytest runners passed. After the added directed tests,
  affected runners were rerun; all 117 cocotb cases pass, including real
  arithmetic and the real/ALTOPS divider variants.
- Built the three committed random-program ELFs, then ran
  `NRET=1 make cosim TARGET=bench`: PASS for all 5 ELFs. Selftest and all three
  random programs pass full RVFI cosim both with and without random stalls;
  stalled canonical CoreMark passes CRC/UART/bounds checks.
- Canonical CoreMark start marker: 14,091; stop marker: 3,843,578.
  Timed cycles: 3,829,487, matching the immediate-recovery parent. All five
  canonical CRCs match, the validation literal is present, EBREAK completes,
  and the simulator reports no out-of-bounds accesses.
- `python3 -m tools.eval.gowin bench --all-options`: all placements pass.
  Options 0/1/2 report 50.431 / 50.384 / 50.384 MHz. Median: 50.384 MHz.
  Option-0 area: 3,615 logic, 905 registers, 8 LUTRAM, 6 BSRAM, 6 DSP.
  Its worst path is inside the unchanged divider at 25.123 ns; options 1/2
  likewise remain divider-limited at approximately 25.142 ns.
- Fitness from the measured median and marker cycles:
  `50.384e6 * 10 / 3829487 = 131.568536`, or 131.57 iter/s.
  This is below the required 140.78114 (approximately 53.914 MHz at unchanged
  cycles), so this hypothesis is a performance regression, not an improvement.

## Concerns

No correctness failure remains in the completed local gates. Removing the
live comparator from queue/decode controls did not improve the scored median
Fmax: the unchanged divider remains critical, and placement changed its
delay. No unrelated datapath optimization was attempted to compensate.

title: Absorb the leading nibble at divider launch to fold the body to four steps
motivation:
LESSONS.md is absent. The champion scores 134.59 iter/sec at 51.54 MHz
with 3,829,487 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its reported worst path is
the shared five-step restoring divider. Structural history shows that
folding eight restoring steps to five improved fitness substantially,
while radix-4 retiming and the recent separate leading-byte stage did
not clear the acceptance margin. Full spatial replication also hurt
routing. The next opportunity is to keep the simple shared radix-2
recurrence but perform a small bounded prefix on the launch edge,
reducing recurring depth without increasing the seven-RUN latency.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Retiming the shared divider around its initially zero remainder should
reduce the timed arithmetic depth: process the first four dividend bits
at the accepted launch edge, then reuse exactly four full-width radix-2
restoring cells on each of seven RUN edges. This consumes 4+7*4=32 bits
and preserves result_valid immediately after launch L plus seven clocks.
Keep a single quotient, remainder and divisor register bank, the existing
IDLE/RUN/DONE protocol, and the existing EX pipeline integration.

At launch form the leading nibble P of the unsigned dividend magnitude
directly from the raw forwarded operand, without waiting for its full
32-bit negation. For a negative signed dividend,
P = (~a[31:28] + (a[27:0] == 0)) modulo 16; otherwise P=a[31:28].
Compute the full magnitude independently for the remaining 28 bits.
A nonzero prefix quotient is possible only when divisor magnitude D
fits four bits. Derive this predicate and the low divisor nibble directly
from raw b and the captured signed-operation condition, rather than from
the full-width magnitude carry chain. For negative signed b, D fits a
nibble exactly when b[31:4] is all ones and b[3:0] is nonzero, and its
nibble is (0-b[3:0]) modulo 16. For other b, D fits when b[31:4]==0.
Zero divisor uses the small-divisor path.

Use four narrow restoring cells to compute unsigned divmod(P,D[3:0])
when D fits a nibble. Each cell uses a five-bit subtraction for the
combined comparison and candidate remainder. Otherwise prefix quotient
is zero and prefix remainder is P. Capture quotient_q as
{dividend_magnitude[27:0], prefix_quotient[3:0]} and remainder_q as
zero_extend(prefix_remainder). Capture full divisor magnitude and the
existing sign/operation flags on that same launch edge. This avoids
full-width work in the prefix and does not add a preparation clock,
divisor multiples, a radix-16 trial bank, or spatial register duplication.

RUN groups zero through five each register the fourth cell's quotient
and remainder. Group six uses that fourth cell's completed outputs for
parallel quotient/remainder sign restoration, result selection and DONE.
Do not use stale state or execute padding bits. The four-cell final group
plus sign correction and the forwarded launch prefix are timing risks;
score all Gowin placements before claiming improvement. Real arithmetic
and RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS must retain exactly the same seven-RUN schedule;
preserve each captured ALTOPS subtraction/XOR expression unchanged.

Preserve all RV32M corner cases. For D=0 the narrow prefix emits four
quotient ones and remainder P, and the body emits the remaining 28 ones
while reconstructing the dividend magnitude. Keep quotient negation
disabled for zero divisor, dividend-only remainder sign restoration,
DIV(INT_MIN,-1)=INT_MIN and REM(INT_MIN,-1)=0. Preserve rejected starts,
simultaneous consume/relaunch, reset cancellation and stable DONE results.
Keep EX operand/RVFI capture, single publication, memory backpressure,
held-WB forwarding, the nine-cycle consecutive-divide and ten-cycle
redirect-to-divide retirement bounds, decoder legality, nret=1 ports,
strict retirement order and every existing correctness assertion.

This is one divider launch/recurrence retiming hypothesis. Require the

timing. The expected eight-percent gain assumes unchanged CoreMark
cycles and a shorter divider path; existing RF/EX and load/control paths
may cap frequency. Acceptance requires fitness above 140.78114 iter/sec,
approximately 53.914 MHz median Fmax at the champion cycle count.
