title: Four-entry loop-exit predictor supplements folded-PC direction prediction
motivation:
LESSONS.md is absent. The champion already has a 64x2 folded-PC bimodal predictor and a two-entry fetch queue. Prior broad tagged target prediction used substantial storage for little additional cycle benefit. Delayed training and delayed squash both regressed, with the unchanged divider remaining critical. Another recovery retiming attempt has weak support.

A local architectural trace of the canonical 2K, ten-iteration program contains 529,588 timed conditional branches, 13,735 JALRs and no timed division operations. An direction model that updates counters in program order has 41,566 misses for the current folded bimodal predictor. Agreement encoding barely improves this, to 41,175, and small gshare tables worsen it. A generic four-entry fully associative loop-count supplement reduces modeled misses to 31,276, nearly matching an eight-entry version's 31,278. Stable loop exits are therefore the strongest small predictor opportunity found, without a large local-history pattern table.

These are architectural trace-model results from an existing simulator build, not measurements of a candidate implementation. They exclude speculative fetch lookahead, queue timing and placement effects. The modeled reduction is about 25 percent of direction misses but only a small fraction of total cycles; it does not establish a gain above the 4.6 percent acceptance margin.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one compact loop-exit predictor alongside the existing folded-PC bimodal fallback. Use exactly four fully associative entries keyed by the full architectural branch PC. Each entry has valid, a 32-bit PC tag, an 8-bit running taken count, an 8-bit learned taken-trip count, a 2-bit confidence counter and an overflow flag. There is no target cache: the current fetched instruction continues to supply the exact B/J immediate and alignment check. Use four parallel valid-qualified tag comparisons and one-hot selection, rather than a serial priority chain in the fetch-PC path. Approximately 210 state bits, including replacement control, are sufficient.

At fetch, a legal word-aligned backward conditional branch may override the bimodal direction only on a valid tag hit with confidence at least two, a nonzero learned trip count and no overflow. Predict not taken precisely when the running taken count equals the learned trip count; otherwise predict taken. Every miss, low-confidence entry, forward branch, overflowed entry and ineligible encoding uses the existing predictor. JAL remains directly predicted and JALR remains resolved in EX. Continue to train the original 64x2 table toward actual direction for every accepted eligible conditional branch, preserving its index, weakly-taken reset and local Boolean saturation logic.

Train loop state only at the existing accepted, legal, nontrapping EX conditional-branch boundary, using the resolving instruction's registered PC, immediate sign and fully forwarded actual condition. A backward-branch tag miss allocates the first invalid entry, or the round-robin victim when all four entries are valid. Advance the two-bit replacement pointer only on an allocation that evicts a valid entry; do not pin confident entries. Initialize a new entry's running count to one for taken or zero for not taken, learned trip count and confidence to zero, and overflow to zero.

For a matching accepted taken branch, increment its running count. At 255, set overflow and clear confidence instead of wrapping; keep overflow set until a not-taken outcome. On a matching not-taken branch, an unoverflowed nonzero running count that equals the learned trip count increments confidence with saturation at three. Otherwise install the observed count as the learned trip count and clear confidence; after overflow install zero. Then clear running count and overflow. This learns an exit only after repeated equal completed trips, adapts to variable bounds and handles loops longer than the counter range safely. Never truncate PC tags or seed entries with benchmark addresses, counts or results.

Use committed EX updates only: do not add speculative iteration counters, rollback checkpoints or a training bypass. Fetch and training on the same edge observe old loop state. title: Radix-4 then radix-8 trials shorten five-bit divider groups
motivation:
LESSONS.md is absent. The champion scores 134.59 iter/sec at 51.540 MHz
and 3,829,487 bracketed cycles. Its reported worst path is entirely
inside the five-cell restoring divider, at 24.838 ns across 152 cells.
Earlier radix-4 groups reduced arithmetic depth but left three or four
dependent levels; segmented borrow lookahead regressed severely, and
the launch-prefix and forwarding-predecode attempts also regressed.
A wider parallel-trial digit offers a different local arithmetic trade:
replace the five serial subtract/select cells with only two levels,
while preserving the proven instruction and divider schedules.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Rewrite only div_unit's real RUN arithmetic as a radix-4 digit followed
by a radix-8 digit for each of the six normal five-bit groups. The last
group consumes exactly the remaining two bits with an independent copy
of the current two radix-2 cells and fused sign restoration. Preserve accepted launch, seven RUN edges,
held DONE, consume, operand capture and all CPU pipeline boundaries.
This is one local parallel-trial divider optimization, with no new
execution stage or instruction-latency change.

Capture unsigned divisor magnitude D and explicitly widened unsigned
35-bit odd multiples 3D, 5D and 7D at launch. Form 3D=(D<<1)+D,
5D=(D<<2)+D and 7D=(D<<3)-D in parallel, using 35-bit D before every
shift or arithmetic operation. Derive 2D and 4D by wiring shifts of D
and 6D by shifting registered 3D. No divisor-multiple generation may
remain in the recurring RUN chain. Avoid computing an odd multiple
by cascading the other odd multiples. Check the forwarded launch path
through magnitude and multiple generation in vendor timing.

The radix-8 cell follows the radix-4 cell and forms unsigned 35-bit
T={R[31:0],Q[31:29]} from its completed remainder and quotient. Compute
T-kD for k=1..7 in parallel as explicitly zero-extended 36-bit
subtractions, deriving success ok[k] from !difference[k][35]. Set
ok[0]=1 and ok[8]=0. The disjoint winning mask for digit k=0..7 is
ok[k] && !ok[k+1]. Select the low 32 remainder bits from T for digit
zero or the corresponding difference for other digits using masked
OR. Encode the three appended quotient bits as
{ok[4], (ok[2] && !ok[4]) || ok[6],
 (ok[1] && !ok[2]) || (ok[3] && !ok[4]) ||
 (ok[5] && !ok[6]) || ok[7]}. Use parallel selection, not a serial seven-way priority chain.
For nonzero D the selected remainder is less than D and fits 32 bits.
For D=0 digit seven wins, preserving the original dividend prefix.

The radix-4 cell similarly forms 34-bit T={R[31:0],Q[31:30]} and uses
parallel 35-bit subtractions of D, 2D and 3D with disjoint masked-OR
selection, then appends the two-bit digit
{ok[2], ok[3] || (ok[1] && !ok[2])}. Its inputs are the registered
quotient and remainder; it consumes the first two bits of a normal group
and feeds the radix-8 cell that consumes the next three bits. Register
the radix-8 cell outputs for groups zero through five. Preserve a
physically separate terminal path consisting of the current two radix-2
cells driven directly by quotient_q/remainder_q. Sign-correct only that
terminal path, select quotient or remainder and enter DONE at group six.
Do not place a normal/terminal input mux ahead of a shared digit cell: a
static timing tool still times its inactive normal-group arithmetic into
the final negation, which regressed the first local probe.
Do not process padding bits or use stale pre-terminal registers.

Preserve quotient-negation suppression for a zero divisor, remainder
sign from the dividend only, all DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU results including
INT_MIN/-1 and divisors with bit 31 set, reset cancellation, rejected
starts, simultaneous consume/relaunch and stable result retention.
Preserve the exact captured ALTOPS subtraction/XOR expressions and
seven-clock completion in the formal build. EX forwarding and RVFI
operand capture, single publication, memory backpressure, held-WB
provenance, decoder legality, nret=1 IO, retirement order and symbolic
progress remain unchanged. Existing nine-cycle consecutive-divide and
ten-cycle redirect-to-divide retirement checks must continue to pass.

Validate the actual divider with an independent integer oracle and
retain every existing correctness gate. Score canonical marker-bracketed
CoreMark cycles, CRCs/UART and median Gowin Fmax under the existing
stalls. Parallel trials increase LUT area and divisor fanout; the
launch and live-load/ALU paths can cap frequency. A temporary implementation with this digit order and the separate
terminal path passed full-core Verilator lint and the existing real
and ALTOPS divider tests and
measured 51.069/53.299/53.299 MHz across Gowin placement options, median
53.299 MHz, using 4,059 LUTs and 1,004 FFs. This is a local timing probe,
not a completed formal/cosim/CoreMark evaluation. The implied clock gain
is about 3.41 percent and does not yet clear the acceptance margin;
at unchanged cycles this projects roughly 139.18 iter/sec. The remaining
worst paths cross memory, integer forwarding and ALU logic. The forecast
therefore remains low-confidence rather than claiming an accepted result. At unchanged cycles acceptance
requires fitness above 140.78114 iter/sec and median Fmax above about
53.914 MHz, beyond the 4.6 percent acceptance margin.

title: Six-stage operand-register pipeline cuts live bypass-to-execute paths
motivation:
LESSONS.md is absent. The champion scores 134.59 iter/sec at 51.540 MHz
and 3,829,487 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Structural history already
covers divider folding, multiplier operand isolation and the fetch
queue. Recent divider and prediction changes have exposed competing
RF-to-multiply and live MEM-load-to-integer/redirect paths.

A local scratch probe retimed divider completion into EX publication:
a two-bit launch prefix, seven four-bit groups and a final two-bit/sign
combinational result. It passed the existing real/ALTOPS divider and EX
tests, and a separate arithmetic model passed 60,392 operand pairs.
Gowin placement options 0/1/2 reached only 50.082/49.777/49.777 MHz.
The divider disappeared from the five worst paths; those paths instead
crossed RF or live dmem data, operand forwarding and execution. This
probe is evidence against a divider-only hypothesis, not a measured
result for the proposed six-stage core. Registering the fully forwarded
operands can cut the remaining execution cones, provided the divider
and its launch/publication boundaries are aligned with that pipeline.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Repartition execution as IF -> ID -> OF -> EX -> MEM -> WB, introducing
one operand-forwarding register before the integer, branch and multiply
execution logic. This is one structural pipeline retiming hypothesis:
source lookup/selection belongs to OF, arithmetic and branch resolution
read only OF/EX registers, and division is launched from OF when possible
with its final arithmetic registered directly at EX/MEM publication.
Keep single issue and nret=1. No cache or prediction-policy change is
included.

ID registers instruction, PC, immediate, validated controls, source
addresses, destination, prediction and validity. Move architectural RF
reads to OF, addressed by those registered source addresses, and capture
source values only on actual OF acceptance. A held OF instruction must
reread the current RF and current valid bypass sources; it must never
depend on a raw value captured before an older WB write. Preserve RF
write-first and x0 semantics. OF/EX stores both resolved source values
and their RVFI metadata; EX uses those registered values without a live
forwarding mux or live dmem connection to its ALU, multiplier, comparator
or JALR adder.

OF resolves each source in youngest-writer order: the current accepted
EX instruction's actual result, then the valid MEM instruction's
registered ALU result or aligned/sign-extended live load, then WB,
then RF. Expose EX's pre-register writeback result for this path,
including PC+4 links and completed division. A back-to-back ALU or
multiply dependency forwards EX result into the OF/EX operand register
at the same edge that writes EX/MEM; no extra dependency bubble is
required. Suppress producers that are invalid, illegal, misaligned,
nonwriters or rd=x0. A load in EX cannot forward data yet: interlock
only when the valid OF instruction actually uses its nonzero rd,
hold ID/OF and fetch-head consumption, and insert an OF/EX validity
bubble while that load advances to MEM. On the next accepting edge,
capture the correct MEM load value. Use decoded actual-source enables
so immediate bits never produce false dependencies. This replaces
immediate live MEM-to-executing-EX consumption with MEM-to-OF capture.

dmem backpressure freezes EX/MEM and both younger payload registers,
clears MEM/WB validity once as today, and preserves WB provenance.
Divide wait holds younger instructions while older MEM/WB drains once.
Maintain separate payload holds and validity kills. When inserting a
load bubble, advance the older EX load exactly once. An accepted EX
redirect clears both younger ID/OF and OF/EX validity plus all fetch
occupancy, with priority over a younger dependency or queue hold.
Preserve accepted-execution branch training, the original prediction
carried by each fetched word, and exact branch/JALR trap/target checks.
Branch resolution moves one stage later and must squash every younger
instruction before memory or RF side effects.

Align the divider with the new operand boundary rather than adding a
retirement clock. When a legal DIV/REM transfers from OF and the engine
is idle, launch it at that same edge using OF's fully resolved operands;
capture instruction, PC, controls and exact RVFI sources together.
The older EX instruction may advance normally on this edge. Transfer
ownership to EX's divide-active state and hold its OF/EX instruction
until publication. If early launch is unavailable, let the instruction
enter EX and launch from its registered operands at the next accepting
edge. In particular, a second divide entering EX on the prior divide's
consume edge launches on the following edge, preserving the existing
nine-cycle consecutive-divide retirement gap. Early OF launch offsets
the added operand stage on recovery-to-divide paths, retaining the
existing ten-cycle bound. Launch must be gated by actual OF acceptance,
older MEM acceptance, reset and accepted EX redirects.

Physically separate early-divider operand selection from the general
OF capture mux. Its EX bypass uses only the normal non-divide EX result,
plus registered MEM/WB or RF sources; never connect completed divider
arithmetic to this launch mux. The engine is not idle when a divide
publishes, so that case uses EX fallback after OF/EX captures the
completed value. Merely gating an early start does not remove a static
final-divider-to-OF-to-magnitude timing path. Keep the general OF mux's
completed-DIV bypass for ordinary consumers, but expose normal EX result
and final division as separate internal signals. The fallback launch
reads only registered OF/EX values.

Use the scratch-probed divider retiming so the old five-step recurrence
does not cap the new pipeline. At launch L, consume the magnitude's
leading two bits with two narrow restoring cells. For D>3 emit zero
prefix quotient and retain prefix remainder P. For D<=3, including
zero, compute exact narrow divmod(P,D). Form P directly from raw a:
for negative signed a, P=(~a[31:30]+(a[29:0]==0)) modulo four;
otherwise P=a[31:30]. A negative signed b has magnitude <=3 iff
b[31:2] is all ones and b[1:0]!=0; its small magnitude is
(0-b[1:0]) modulo four. Otherwise D<=3 iff b[31:2]==0.
Capture the low thirty dividend-magnitude bits independently and seed
Q={magnitude_low30,prefix_quotient}; capture full divisor magnitude,
zero-extended prefix remainder and existing signs/op flags.

Seven RUN edges L+1..L+7 each register four ordinary full-width
subtract/restore steps: thirty bits have then been consumed including
the prefix. Enter READY after L+7, hold all arithmetic state and expose
the last two steps plus parallel sign restoration combinationally.
EX/MEM registers that final result at consume edge L+8; remove the
intervening divider completed-result register. Exactly 2+7*4+2=32 bits
are processed. READY result and valid remain stable for any delayed
consume, rejected starts or changing live inputs. Preserve reset and
standalone simultaneous consume/relaunch. The final path reads the
held thirty-bit state, never the four-step feedback output.

Real arithmetic and RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS have identical launch-to-valid
and publication schedules. Retain every exact ALTOPS expression,
RV32M signed/unsigned result, zero-divisor result, quotient-negation
suppression on zero, dividend-only remainder sign, and INT_MIN/-1
behavior. Capture divide metadata at whichever launch edge actually
accepts its operands, without allowing a changing forward source to
corrupt held RVFI state.

Preserve all top-level memory and nret=1 RVFI ports, decoder default
illegal and EBREAK-only SYSTEM rules, target/access traps, oldest-first
retirement, +1 order, outstanding request stability and one-time side
effects. Do not weaken existing formal, arithmetic, publication,
nine/ten-cycle progress, cosim, CRC, UART, bounds or marker checks.

The shorter execution cones must compensate for a restored one-cycle
load-use interlock and one additional branch recovery stage. An initial
budget is about 6-7 percent more CoreMark cycles; at seven percent more
cycles, clearing the 4.6 percent acceptance margin requires median
Fmax above approximately 57.686 MHz. A 60-62 MHz outcome would yield
roughly 9-12 percent better fitness. This full-pipeline forecast is
unmeasured and low confidence. OF's EX-result bypass, divider launch,
final-result-to-EX mux and placement are the main timing risks. Require
the final implemented core to pass every unchanged correctness gate and
exceed 140.78114 iter/sec using actual marker-bracketed cycles and
median Gowin Fmax across all placement options.

title: Committed link-register shadow predicts returns without a target table
motivation:
LESSONS.md is absent. The folded-PC bimodal predictor already handles
direct branches and JAL, while every aligned JALR still redirects in EX.
The prior 64-entry tagged target predictor regressed substantially;
delayed training and registered squash also lost clock speed. The recent
four-entry loop predictor saved only 12,677 of 3,829,487 cycles and lost
median Fmax, so adding another associative direction supplement has weak
support. A local architectural trace contains 13,735 timed JALRs, all
conventional jalr x0,x1,0 returns. Their targets change with callers,
making a committed shadow of x1 a smaller, more direct target source
than a PC-tagged last-target table. A separately compiled canonical
-O3, 2K, ten-iteration ELF passes all five CRCs in the architectural
reference and confirms this count. Delaying its latest x1 write by one
through four architectural instructions still predicts all 13,735
targets; delays of five or six miss one. This instruction-order model
excludes speculative lookahead, bus stalls and hardware timing, so it
is supporting evidence rather than a scored implementation result.

title: Two radix-4 body digits with narrow divider bootstrap
motivation:
LESSONS.md is absent. The current champion scores 146.77 iter/sec at
59.068 MHz with 4,024,573 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its worst Gowin
path runs from remainder_q to remainder_q inside div_unit, crossing
128 cells with a 22.272 ns arrival time. Every body clock currently
cascades four full-width radix-2 subtract/restore steps. Earlier
parallel-trial attempts shortened divider paths but encountered live
load/ALU forwarding limits; the champion's new OF/EX operand registers
remove that competing cone. Segmented borrow lookahead regressed badly,
so preserve native carry arithmetic and halve the dependent body digits.
An isolated implementation of this exact two-digit/narrow-bootstrap
design passes full-core Verilator lint and the existing divider suite
in both real and ALTOPS modes, extended with every six-bit dividend
prefix and divisors around the 63/64 bootstrap boundary. Three Gowin
placement options measured 58.836/61.916/61.916 MHz: median 61.916 MHz,
4,486 LUT4s and 963 registers. The median clock gain is 4.82 percent;
this is a timing probe, not a scored CoreMark or formal evaluation.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Optimize only the real combinational divider recurrence: replace the
recurring four radix-2 body steps with two radix-4 parallel-trial
digits. Preserve the two-bit launch prefix, seven RUN edges, held READY
state, independent final two-bit/sign result path, early/fallback EX
launch, and existing instruction latency. This changes arithmetic within
the existing registers; it adds no CPU stage or stall policy.

Keep divisor magnitude D captured at launch. On the first RUN edge,
register the existing explicitly widened 34-bit 3D = D + (D << 1),
exactly as today, so launch never gains a magnitude-to-multiple carry
chain. The first RUN group must use a separate narrow four-bit bootstrap
rather than the radix-4 body, since registered 3D is not available yet.
At that group's input, the existing launch prefix guarantees R <= 3.
For D[31:6] != 0, all four quotient bits are zero and the resulting
remainder is {R[1:0], Q[31:28]}; D is at least 64 while this window is
at most 63. Otherwise compute exactly four restoring steps using a
six-bit remainder and six-bit divisor, with seven-bit zero-extended
trial subtractions and borrow-controlled restoration. Never use a
full-width subtractor in this bootstrap. Append those four quotient
bits to Q[27:0]. Use it only when group_q == 0, retaining the full D
register and all existing launch sign flags. D=0 must emit four ones
and retain the original dividend prefix.

On groups 1 through 6 use two identical radix-4 cells in series, each
consuming two dividend bits and appending two quotient bits. A cell
forms the unsigned 34-bit window T={R[31:0],Q[31:30]}. Compute T-D,
T-2D and T-3D in parallel as 35-bit zero-extended subtractions, with
D and 2D explicitly widened to 34 bits and 3D read from its register.
Bit 34 indicates borrow. Let ok1, ok2, ok3 be the no-borrow predicates;
append {ok2, ok3 | (ok1 & !ok2)}. Select the low 32 remainder bits
using disjoint masks !ok1, ok1 & !ok2, ok2 & !ok3, and ok3 applied
to T and the corresponding differences. Express this as parallel
masked OR, avoiding a serial priority mux and a compare followed by
a separate subtraction. Retain high trial and multiple bits until
borrow detection; restored R fits 32 bits for all nonzero divisors.
With D=0 all trials succeed, digit three wins, and remainder retains
the dividend magnitude. Two cells consume exactly four bits per RUN
edge. Together with the first four-bit bootstrap and two-bit launch,
seven groups process exactly thirty dividend bits before READY.

Select bootstrap versus ordinary body only at the quotient/remainder
register inputs. The existing final two-bit lookahead and parallel
sign-restoration network must continue reading held quotient_q and
remainder_q directly, never a bootstrap/body output or input mux.
Keep its existing registered triple divisor source. Preserve its
direct result publication into EX/MEM and OF forwarding, stable READY
retention, consume/relaunch, rejected starts and reset cancellation.
All real and RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS builds retain the exact seven-RUN-edge
result_valid schedule; retain every ALTOPS formula unchanged.

Preserve signed remainder from the dividend, zero-divisor suppression
of quotient negation, DIV(INT_MIN,-1)=INT_MIN, REM(INT_MIN,-1)=0 and
all full-width unsigned operands. Preserve nret=1 IO, decoder legality,
retirement order, symbolic progress, memory handshakes, held-WB
provenance, wrong-path suppression and every correctness gate. The
predicted gain is higher frequency with unchanged CoreMark cycles.

body. Parallel subtractor area/fanout and this remaining path limit

title: Retimed two-digit radix-4 divider with parallel terminal publication
motivation:
The six-stage champion scores 146.77 iter/sec at 59.068 MHz and
4,024,573 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its worst reported path is now
entirely inside div_unit, remainder_q back to remainder_q: 22.272 ns
and 128 cells. Four dependent full-width subtract/restore cells remain
on every RUN feedback path. The operand-stage change removed the live
RF/load execution paths that limited earlier parallel-trial experiments.

The structural history has been checked. r4s1 used three radix-4 cells;
r6s1 used a leading byte and two radix-4 cells, but both were limited by
RF/MEM execution paths. r7s1 regressed because four restoring cells fed
final sign correction. Preserve the champion's short two-bit launch
and separate terminal publication, and specialize the first RUN edge
for narrow prefix arithmetic plus divisor preparation. Subsequent RUN
edges can then reuse just two full-width radix-4 cells, with no added
CPU stage or divide latency.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Restructure the shared divider into three physically distinct paths:
the existing two-bit launch, a narrow first RUN/preparation stage, and
a two-cell radix-4 feedback body, followed by the existing independent
held-state terminal two-bit/sign path. Preserve accepted launch L,
seven RUN edges L+1..L+7, READY after L+7 and EX/MEM consumption at L+8.
This is one structural specialization and folding hypothesis; retain the
six-stage CPU, fetch queue, predictor, nret=1 and all memory interfaces.

Keep the exact two-bit launch-prefix logic, low-thirty-bit magnitude,
full divisor magnitude and captured sign/op flags. At RUN group zero,
L+1, the input remainder has only two significant bits. Consume the
next four dividend bits with four narrow restoring cells. The complete
six-bit prefix is at most 63: if D[31:6]!=0, append four quotient zeros
and set R={old_R[1:0],old_Q[31:28]}; otherwise use D[5:0] in four
seven-bit unsigned subtract/restore steps. Each narrow difference's
bit six is borrow; retain six remainder bits and shift Q by one at
each step. At this edge register Q={old_Q[27:0],new_digit} and the
zero-extended six-bit remainder. D=0 must append four quotient ones
and retain the prefix as remainder. Do not feed full-width multiple
preparation into the live launch logic.

At L+1 also register explicitly widened unsigned 34-bit
3D=zero_extend(D)+(zero_extend(D)<<1), from captured divisor_q.
Generate D and 2D by zero extension and wiring shifts. This preparation
runs beside the narrow prefix stage and adds no execution clock.
No divisor-multiple addition belongs in the recurring RUN datapath.

On RUN groups one through six, L+2..L+7, reuse exactly two dependent
radix-4 digit cells. Each forms unsigned 34-bit T={R,Q[31:30]} and
computes T-D, T-2D and T-3D as independent zero-extended 35-bit
subtractions. Let ok1,ok2,ok3 be clear borrow bits. Append the digit
{ok2, ok3 | (ok1 & !ok2)}. Select the low 32 remainder bits with
parallel disjoint masks !ok1, ok1 & !ok2, ok2 & !ok3, and ok3 on T
and the respective differences. Use masked OR rather than cascaded
priority selection. Cell two reads cell one's restored state; register
only cell two's Q/R after each full four-bit group. Preserve all high
multiple and trial bits until borrow detection. For nonzero D, restored
R<D fits 32 bits; for D=0 every digit is three and the remainder
reconstructs the dividend magnitude.

After L+7 exactly thirty bits have been processed:
2 launch + 4 first-RUN prefix + 6*4 feedback. Keep final two-bit
lookahead physically independent of the feedback cells. It reads held quotient_q/remainder_q and the registered D/3D,
and publishes directly into EX/MEM at L+8. Prepare all four possible
signed architectural results in parallel before selecting the final
digit, so late borrow decisions do not feed sign or operation muxes.
Do not feed RUN outputs or a prefix/body selection mux into terminal
arithmetic, introduce padding bits, add a result register or extend
latency. READY state, data and valid remain stable during delayed consume,
changing live inputs and rejected starts.

For terminal T={held_R,held_Q[31:30]}, retain widened parallel
T-D, T-2D and T-3D differences and their borrow-derived success bits.
Use disjoint terminal masks !ok1, ok1 & !ok2, ok2 & !ok3, and ok3.
For each constant final digit k=0..3, prepare positive remainder
(T-kD)[31:0] and negative remainder (kD-T)[31:0] in parallel, with
k=0 using T and -T. Prepare quotient {held_Q[29:0],2'(k)} and its
negative: for k=0 use {(30'd0-held_Q[29:0]),2'b00}; for k>0 use
{~held_Q[29:0],(2'd0-2'(k))}. These are exact constant-digit negations,
including the upper carry when k=0. Captured remainder/quotient sign
and select_rem flags choose one architectural result per candidate
before the final masks. Publish the masked OR of those four candidates.
This replaces the terminal priority mux followed by sign/op selection
with a parallel result bank at the same publication boundary; no
selected digit drives a new wide negate or post-selection sign mux.

Preserve start/busy/result_valid/consume, simultaneous consume/relaunch,
reset cancellation, early OF launch, registered EX fallback, isolated
early-divider operand selection and exactly one publication. Real and
RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS builds retain the same seven-RUN schedule and every
exact existing subtraction/XOR formula. Preserve all RV32M results,
zero-divisor suppression of quotient negation, dividend-only remainder
sign, INT_MIN/-1, exact RVFI operands/order, and outstanding memory
requests. Retain all existing nine-cycle consecutive-divide and
ten-cycle redirect-to-divide assertions, decoder legality, nret=1 ports,
formal/cosim/CRC/UART/address-bound/marker checks.

publication passed existing real/ALTOPS divider tests, EX-divider tests
and the full pipeline test runner. Gowin placement options 0/1/2 measured
62.203/62.337/62.337 MHz, median 62.337 MHz, using 4,438 LUTs and
963 FFs, versus the champion's 4,292 LUTs and 963 FFs. At unchanged

percent gain. The feedback-only version reached 62.021 MHz; preparing
signed terminal candidates before digit selection improved publication
margin without altering completion timing. The scratch core also passed
full-RVFI selftest cosim both without stalls and with --istall/--dstall. Its canonical 2K, ten-iteration,

fitness projection uses a measured unchanged iteration/cycle rate.

title: Sixteen tagged history exceptions supplement folded-PC branch prediction
motivation:
LESSONS.md is absent. The champion already predicts direct branches and
JAL with a folded-PC 64-entry bimodal table. Prior target prediction,
delayed training, delayed squash, loop-exit prediction and return-shadow
prediction regressed. A canonical architectural trace has 529,588 timed
conditional branches and 41,566 folded-bimodal direction misses. Larger
bimodal tables, small local-history tables and untagged gshare offer
little improvement or worsen aliasing. A small tagged exception table
can learn correlated hard cases without replacing the successful base
predictor or storing branch targets.

A local replay of the canonical -O3, 2K, ten-iteration architectural
trace models both bus-ready draws, the current six pipeline stages,
two fetch entries, branch recovery, load-use interlocks and divider
launch. It reproduces the champion's 4,024,573 marker-bracketed cycles
exactly. Sixteen tagged entries with 16-bit accepted history model
4,005,415 cycles; 32 and 64 entries model 4,002,999 and 4,002,603.
The smallest table retains most of this modest cycle benefit while
reducing the lookup and training footprint. These are replay results,
not candidate RTL correctness or FPGA timing measurements.

bimodal tables, small local-history tables and untagged gshare offer
little improvement or worsen aliasing. A small tagged exception table
can learn correlated hard cases without replacing the successful base
predictor or storing branch targets.

A local replay of the canonical -O3, 2K, ten-iteration architectural
trace models both bus-ready draws, the current six pipeline stages,
two fetch entries, branch recovery, load-use interlocks and divider
launch. It reproduces the champion's 4,024,573 marker-bracketed cycles
exactly. Sixteen tagged entries with 16-bit accepted history model
4,005,415 cycles; 32 and 64 entries model 4,002,999 and 4,002,603.

reducing the lookup and training footprint. These are replay results,
not candidate RTL correctness or FPGA timing measurements.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one direction-only correlation exception predictor: keep the current
64x2 folded-PC bimodal table as the base and add a fixed 16-entry tagged
table indexed by branch PC and a 16-bit EX-accepted conditional-outcome
history. Each exception entry contains valid, an eight-bit tag, a
two-bit direction counter and a two-bit confidence counter. Initialize
valid and history to zero; uninitialized entry payloads cannot influence
prediction. The base remains weakly taken with its current hash and
per-entry Boolean saturating updates. This is one predictor enhancement;
retain pipeline depth, arithmetic units and memory organization.

Define P = PC >> 2, H = the registered 16-bit history, base_index =
(P XOR (P >> 6)) & 63, exception_index = the low four bits of
(P XOR (P >> 4) XOR H XOR (H >> 4) XOR (H >> 8) XOR (H >> 12)),
and exception_tag = the low eight bits of
((P >> 4) XOR (P >> 12) XOR H XOR (H >> 4)). Use exactly these generic
hashes, with no benchmark address constants or target truncation.
For legal aligned conditional branches, an exception valid/tag hit
overrides the base only when confidence is nonzero. Otherwise use
the base direction. Keep existing raw legality/alignment predecode,
exact direct targets, unconditional JAL prediction and EX-only JALR
resolution. Lookup uses registered state with no EX training bypass.
The exception bank has only 208 payload/control bits plus 16 history
bits; use four-bit indexed parallel selection without an associative
search or serial priority chain. Prefer explicit per-entry registers
and local decoded writes for this small bank. No target is cached.

Capture the base direction, exception index and exception tag at the
actual fetch acceptance edge along with the chosen predicted_taken bit.
Carry them through both queue entries, empty bypass, IF/ID, ID/OF and
OF/EX; retain them through holds and discard their validity on flush.
Never reconstruct an older instruction's context from current history.
When an accepted legal nontrapping conditional branch reaches EX,
train the existing base as today. For an exception entry whose current
valid bit is set and tag matches the captured index/tag, saturate its direction counter
toward the actual outcome. Increment confidence with saturation at
three when its pre-update counter predicts correctly; otherwise reset
confidence to zero. On a tag miss allocate only if the captured base
prediction was wrong, replacing that indexed entry with the captured
tag, a weak counter toward the actual outcome and confidence zero.
Treat an invalid entry as a tag miss. Revalidate tags at training time:
intervening replacements cannot be
updated as though they belonged to the original context. Each counter
update must read its own registered entry, avoiding a second indexed
counter read mux on the training path.

Shift the actual outcome into H exactly once for each accepted legal
nontrapping conditional branch. Jumps, bubbles, held EX instructions,
wrong-path instructions, reset and trapped branches never update H or
the exception table. History is nonspeculative; fetches can use stale
history while older branches remain in flight, and such guesses recover
normally. No rollback or history checkpoint is needed. A redirect does
not discard the resolving branch's accepted update. Same-edge lookup
and training use old state, and reset overrides all training.

Preserve immediate EX direction-XOR verification and the registered
prediction's choice of recovery address. A correct override creates no
flush; a wrong override discards every younger word and recovers to the
actual direct successor. Keep actual RVFI next PCs, PC+4 link values,
decoder default-illegal behavior, alignment traps, nret=1 IO, strict
retirement order, stalled-WB forwarding and all bus acceptance gates.
Predictor state may only choose fetch direction, never architectural
results or whether an accepted branch receives verification.

The modeled cycle change gives only 0.478 percent more iterations per

replay clears the 4.6-percent acceptance margin. It would need more
than approximately 61.492 MHz median Fmax at the modeled cycle count.
The current divider remains the timing limit; extra lookup/tag logic and placement changes

bounds, canonical CRC/UART and marker-timing checks. Acceptance requires
measured median Gowin Fmax times CoreMark iterations/cycle to exceed
153.52142 iter/sec, the champion's 146.77 plus 4.6 percent.

title: Select OF forwarding sources directly with disjoint one-hot masks
motivation: LESSONS.md is absent. The champion measures 161.60 iter/sec at 65.036 MHz median Gowin Fmax and 4,024,573 bracketed CoreMark cycles. The latest critical path crosses EX/ALU, OF and early divider launch, rather than only the divider feedback cells. Prior micro_opt forwarding-match predecode regressed on the older pipeline, and prior merged EX/ALU mux experiments also regressed. The current six-stage operand-register boundary provides a different target: both OF forwarding networks still encode youngest-writer priority into two-bit selectors and then decode those selectors into wide data muxes. Direct source masks can remove this encoding/decoding round trip while preserving every existing register and acceptance edge.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace only the forwarding selection representation inside operand_stage with direct disjoint source masks. Preserve the same source comparisons and youngest-writer priority, but do not form a two-bit fwd selector and compare or decode it again for data selection. For each nonzero source address compute E = ex_w_en && ex_rd != 0 && ex_rd == source, M = mem_w_en && mem_rd != 0 && mem_rd == source, and W = wb_w_en && wb_rd != 0 && wb_rd == source. For source x0 force E/M/W false and retain the existing explicit zero at capture. Select normal EX using E && ex_normal_w_en, completed DIV using E && !ex_normal_w_en, MEM using !E && M, WB using !E && !M && W, and RF using !E && !M && !W. Form the resolved word as the OR of these five individually masked values. Derive masks in parallel from address hits; avoid an encoded priority mux followed by another decoder.

For the independent early-divider network, compute its own E from ex_early_w_en and select normal EX, MEM, WB and RF with E, !E && M, !E && !M && W and !E && !M && !W. Express this four-source data selection as masked OR too, replacing its case on an encoded selector. Keep the completed-divider result physically absent from this early mux. Do not change ex_early_w_en, producer qualification, alignment checks, the normal_result/producer_result separation, memory-load formatting, WB data selection or RF write-first behavior. A valid younger producer must retain priority during every hold; invalid/trapping producers and rd=x0 must never become sources. Recompute masks while OF is held, and sample data only at the original accepting edge.

Keep the separate normal and early masks for both architectural sources, existing raw RVFI operands, load-use interlock, early_payload, OF/EX register layout, payload capture enable and validity-only flush behavior. Leave forward_unit available for standalone clients; operand_stage can implement direct masks locally rather than extending unrelated interfaces. Preserve exact real and ALTOPS division behavior and seven-RUN schedule, accepted early/fallback launch, held READY, single publication, nine-cycle divide spacing, ten-cycle redirect-to-divide checks, all memory stalls, wrong-path suppression, held-WB provenance, decoder default-illegal rules, alignment traps, nret=1 IO and +1 RVFI retirement order. A scratch implementation of these direct masks passes the existing operand-stage, EX-divider and pipeline pytest runners. Full-RVFI selftest cosim passes both without stalls and with independent instruction/data stalls. title: EX-only divider launch with a six-clock asymmetric engine
motivation:
The champion scores 161.60 iter/sec at 65.036 MHz and 4,024,573
marker-bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its worst Gowin path crosses EX
arithmetic, OF forwarding and early-divider launch preprocessing,
ending at remainder_q after 20.938 ns. The successful r8s1 operand
register isolates normal execution, but division still bypasses that
boundary. LESSONS.md is absent. Structural history shows that divider
retiming succeeds when preparation and terminal arithmetic are kept
physically separate; r7s1's fused terminal/sign path regressed.
Eliminating early OF launch can remove the remaining arithmetic-to-
forwarding-to-divider chain if one internal divider clock is recovered.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Launch DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU exclusively from registered OF/EX operands
and reduce the engine from seven RUN clocks to six. Recover that
clock by repartitioning prefix work: four bits at launch, six narrow
bits at the first RUN edge, five four-bit body clocks and the existing
independent terminal two-bit publication. Exactly 4+6+5*4+2=32 bits
are processed. This is one structural launch/stage-boundary change;
retain six CPU stages, single issue, nret=1 and all memory interfaces.

Remove early OF launch and its independent early forwarding datapath.
EX's divider op/a/b ports connect directly to registered in.ctrl.alu_op,
in.rs1_val and in.rs2_val, without early/fallback data selection. Start
once for an accepted valid legal divide when the engine is idle and
the older MEM request can advance. Capture exact RVFI sources and
instruction metadata together at this launch. Retain divider ownership,
older-stage draining, frontend holds, load-use handling, dmem priority,
held completions and single publication. Ordinary OF capture must
still forward normal EX and completed-divide results correctly.

At engine launch L, form the four-bit dividend-magnitude prefix P
directly: for a negative signed dividend, P=(~a[31:28]+
(a[27:0]==0)) modulo sixteen; otherwise P=a[31:28]. Compute the low
twenty-eight magnitude bits and full divisor magnitude independently.
Detect magnitude D<=15 directly from raw b, without waiting for its
full-width negate: negative signed b qualifies iff b[31:4] is all ones
and b[3:0]!=0; otherwise b[31:4] must be zero. The small magnitude is
(0-b[3:0]) modulo sixteen for negative b, otherwise b[3:0]. Process
P with a two-bit divmod lookup followed by one narrow radix-4 cell.
The lookup covers D=0,1,2,3 exactly; D>3 yields zero quotient and its
unchanged two-bit prefix remainder. The second cell uses widened
parallel T-D/T-2D/T-3D trials and disjoint masks. Larger D yields
prefix quotient zero and remainder P. Register Q={magnitude_low28,
prefix_Q}, zero-extended prefix R, divisor, signs and result selection.

Also capture the narrow bootstrap's expensive divisor multiples at L,
independently of prefix arithmetic. Compute m=abs(b)[9:0] directly
from raw b: negative signed b uses (0-b[9:0]) modulo 1024, otherwise
b[9:0]. Register unsigned 13-bit 3m,5m,7m using widened shifts/adds.
For D>1023 the bootstrap ignores these truncated-divisor multiples.
Never compute full-width 3D or let a forwarded operand enter these
adders; their inputs come exclusively from the OF/EX operand flops.

At RUN group zero, L+1, consume six additional dividend bits with two
narrow radix-8 cells and prepare registered unsigned 34-bit 3D in
parallel from divisor_q. The completed prefix has only ten bits.
If D[31:10]!=0, append six quotient zeros and concatenate the old
four-bit remainder with Q[31:26]. Otherwise each cell takes three
bits, trials jD for j=1..7 and chooses the largest successful digit
with disjoint masks. Build D,2D,4D by wiring, use the captured 3m,5m,
7m and derive 6m by shifting captured 3m. Keep all thirteen multiple
bits. Since each window is at most 1023, an eligible trial requires
multiple[12:10]==0 plus no borrow in the eleven-bit zero-extended
window[9:0]-multiple[9:0] subtraction. Preserve this high-bit guard;
truncating a large multiple without it is incorrect. Select ten-bit
restored remainders and three-bit quotient digits with masked ORs.
D=0 produces digit seven and reconstructs the original prefix.
Register Q={old_Q[25:0],six_new_bits} and zero-extended ten-bit R.
Full-width 3D preparation has no connection to these narrow cells.

On groups one through five, L+2..L+6, reuse the champion's two
full-width radix-4 cells, widened parallel trials and masked selection.
Enter READY after L+6 with thirty bits processed. Preserve the
independent held-state terminal two-bit/sign candidate bank and
consume into EX/MEM at L+7. There is no selected-result register,
extra padding step or sign arithmetic after the final digit mux.
Retain reset cancellation, rejected starts, simultaneous standalone
consume/relaunch and stable READY results. Real and ALTOPS builds
must have the identical six-RUN schedule and exact existing formulas.
Preserve divide-by-zero, INT_MIN/-1 and every signed remainder rule.

If a divide enters OF/EX at P, engine launch is P+1 and publication
is P+8, matching the champion's early-launch publication edge.
Consecutive divides improve from nine to eight retirement clocks;
unpredicted redirect-to-divide remains at most ten. Strengthen the
exact standalone latency and consecutive-divide checks to six and
eight respectively; retain the unchanged ten-cycle liveness bound
and all correctness assertions. Rework tests specific to early launch
to verify that an OF-only request cannot launch before OF/EX capture,
including wrong-path cancellation and acceptance under memory stalls.

Scratch EX-only launch without registered narrow multiples passed
real/ALTOPS divider arithmetic, and its canonical stalled CoreMark
produced all required CRCs, validation text, no out-of-bounds accesses
and exactly 4,024,573 bracketed cycles. Its median vendor clock was
only 63.827 MHz: divisor-multiple preparation before bootstrap trials
became the new limit. Capturing those narrow multiples at launch is
therefore essential to this final proposal. Do not infer acceptance
from the scratch checks. Require the final implementation's unchanged
unit/formal/cosim gates and median Gowin fitness above 169.0336 iter/sec,
approximately 68.029 MHz at unchanged cycles. Bootstrap depth, launch
multiple preparation and completed-DIV forwarding remain timing risks.

title: Register predictor squash across the six-stage frontend
motivation:
LESSONS.md is absent. The current champion scores 161.60 iter/sec at
65.036 MHz and 4,024,573 timed CoreMark cycles. Recent loop, return-shadow
and tagged-history predictors saved less than one percent of cycles
but regressed Fmax. Architectural-order replay also finds little
benefit from changing the current table to static-bias agree encoding;
a scratch agree implementation saved only 452 timed cycles and measured
54.944 MHz on placement option zero. Direction accuracy offers limited
remaining headroom, so predictor recovery timing is the stronger angle.

The earlier r6s2 registered-squash proposal regressed on the old pipeline
while its divider remained critical. The current six-stage OF/EX design
and retimed divider create a different opportunity: late recovery now
participates in operand acceptance and early-divider launch controls.
Registering only the younger-instruction squash can break that cone
while preserving the existing immediate PC correction and target-fetch
timing. A scratch implementation of the precise protocol below has
measured median Gowin Fmax 68.231 MHz with exactly unchanged timed
cycles, projecting 169.54 iter/sec, a 4.91 percent fitness gain.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Split the existing accepted EX predictor correction into immediate
fetch-PC redirection and one registered squash bit. Add squash_q in
core.sv: synchronous reset clears it; every other edge captures the
current accepted redirect pulse, including zero on no-event cycles.
Preserve conditional effective_taken XOR captured predicted_taken,
prediction-selected recovery targets and aligned JALR correction.
The immediate redirect controls IF's existing PC register only. It
must no longer flush ID/OF or OF/EX, discard queue occupancy, inhibit
operand acceptance, or gate early-divider launch combinationally.
Branch training remains at its existing accepted EX boundary.

On correction edge T, install redirect_target in the fetch PC, with
reset priority and recovery overriding imem backpressure. Retain the
old queue occupancy and payloads until the following squash cycle.
Younger ID and OF words may advance at T; their architectural validity
will be killed at T+1. Preserve the existing registered-control guard
that disallows early divider launch behind any valid EX branch or
jump. Consequently the wrong-path OF word cannot launch a divide on
T, even though its ordinary operand acceptance is now speculative.

While squash_q is set in the cycle after T, IF ignores both old queue
entries and offers the raw bus word at the already-corrected PC through
the empty bypass. Set head_valid from imem_ready alone in this cycle
and allow fetch_accept regardless of stale queue fullness. At T+1
discard old occupancy. If a fresh word is available and decoded, leave
occupancy zero and advance PC to that word's predicted successor. If
available but unconsumed, save it as the sole head and advance PC once.
If imem is stalled, clear occupancy and hold the corrected PC for retry.
Keep reset above correction and correction above ordinary fetch.
No target register or combinational mux on io_imemAddr is added.

In the registered squash cycle allow ID to accept that fresh target
word into ID/OF; do not flush ID/OF on squash_q. Flush OF/EX validity
and suppress operand_accept on squash_q so the old younger ID/OF word
cannot advance as valid. Keep normal backend/load-use holding rules.
The younger word already in EX must publish an invalid EX/MEM payload
at T+1: gate next_payload.valid with !squash_q while retaining ordinary
wide payload capture. Also qualify ex_accept with !squash_q, thereby
suppressing its normal forwarding producer, load producer, training
and redirect. Qualify early_w_en with !squash_q too. A killed word must
never issue memory traffic, write a register, train, recover or retire.
The older resolving control transfer in MEM continues normally.

Replace the live !redirect term in early_start with !squash_q and
retain the existing exclusion of valid EX branches/jumps. Gate both
early_start and fallback_start against squash_q, and force div_wait
low while squash_q is active. A killed DIV/REM therefore cannot launch
or freeze fresh-target decode. An active older divide cannot coexist
with an accepted control-transfer correction under the existing EX
ownership rules; assert this property rather than changing divider
arithmetic, latency, publication or consume behavior. Keep normal

title: One parallel radix-16 digit replaces two serial divider body digits
motivation:
The champion scores 174.88 iter/sec at 70.381 MHz with 4,024,573
marker-bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its worst Gowin paths include the
divider's two serial full-width radix-4 digits as well as EX/OF
control. A local champion retest reproduces placement-0 69.480 MHz.
Removing branch comparison from operand capture controls leaves
placement-0 at 69.662 MHz, with the divider now the worst path, so
that control rewrite alone has insufficient acceptance headroom.
LESSONS.md is absent. The micro_opt history shows that segmented
borrow arithmetic and mixed serial radices have failed, whereas
registered parallel trials gained substantial clock speed once
launch and terminal arithmetic were kept separate. The current
six-RUN engine supplies a clean boundary for a single faster digit.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Optimize only the real four-bit divider body recurrence. Replace
each pair of dependent radix-4 cells with one parallel radix-16
restoring digit that consumes four dividend bits. Preserve four-bit
launch, six-bit narrow group-zero bootstrap, five four-bit body
clocks, independent terminal two-bit publication, and the identical
six-RUN real/ALTOPS schedule. No CPU stage, instruction latency,
divider handshake, forwarding or stall-policy change is included.

At group zero, alongside the existing narrow bootstrap and full-width
3D preparation, register explicitly unsigned 36-bit odd multiples
5D, 7D, 9D, 11D, 13D and 15D from captured divisor_q. Keep the existing
34-bit 3D register and zero-extend it to 36 bits for body trials.
Form 5D=D+(D<<2), 7D=(D<<3)-D, 9D=(D<<3)+D and
15D=(D<<4)-D, with D zero-extended to 36 bits before all shifts.
Prepare 11D from the three independent words 8D, 2D, D and 13D
from 8D, 4D, D with a carry-save XOR/majority layer followed by one
36-bit addition: sum=X^Y^Z, carry=((X&Y)|(X&Z)|(Y&Z))<<1,
multiple=sum+carry. Do not cascade general-purpose additions for
these triples. Every odd multiple is prepared directly from D in
parallel, never from another newly computed multiple. Derive all
even multiples by wiring shifts of registered odd multiples or D.
No multiple-generation arithmetic may remain in the recurring body,
launch, or terminal-publication path.

For a body clock form unsigned 36-bit T={remainder_q,
quotient_q[31:28]}. In parallel compute fifteen explicitly
zero-extended 37-bit differences T-kD, k=1..15. Let ok[k] be
!difference[k][36], ok[0]=1 and ok[16]=0. The winning mask for
k=0..15 is ok[k] && !ok[k+1]. Select the low 32 bits of T for
digit zero or the corresponding difference for nonzero digits,
and encode the selected four-bit k. Use disjoint masked data
terms and explicit balanced OR trees for both restored remainder
and digit, avoiding a serial fifteen-way priority mux. Register
Q={old_Q[27:0],digit} and the restored R. For D nonzero,
R<D and T<16D; widened multiples retain every high bit and the
selected R fits 32 bits. For D=0 all trials succeed, digit=15
and R retains the dividend prefix, preserving the current
division/remainder-by-zero behavior without a new special schedule.

Keep the current launch operands/sign flags, group counter,
rejected-start behavior, reset cancellation, held READY state,
simultaneous standalone consume/relaunch, terminal quotient/sign
candidate bank, INT_MIN/-1 handling and signed remainder rules.
Leave every ALTOPS formula and completion edge unchanged. Keep
top-level nret=1 IO, decoder default-illegal rules, alignment
traps, load interlocks, wrong-path suppression, held-WB provenance,

Extend independent divmod arithmetic checks with all sixteen body
digits, transitions around each kD, quotient nibbles spanning body
boundaries, high unsigned divisors, all signs, zero divisors and
overflow. Require existing real/ALTOPS divider, EX and pipeline

unchanged terminal/OF paths are the main risks. At unchanged cycles,

title: Two-stage partial-product multiplier removes the EX-to-OF product path
motivation:
The champion reaches 174.88 iterations/second at 70.381 MHz with
4,024,573 marker-bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its reported worst path
crosses EX arithmetic and OF forwarding, beginning at an OF/EX source
register. The six-stage operand boundary and EX-only divider launch
already removed the larger live-memory and early-divider cones.
Multiplication still computes complete 32x32 products and forwards
them into the next instruction's operand register within one clock.
A registered partial-product boundary can shorten this remaining
path, with extra cycles confined to immediate multiply dependencies.
LESSONS.md is absent. Prior structural attempts in log.jsonl were
checked; none introduced this multiplier pipeline. The recent direct
one-hot OF forwarding proposal regressed, so retain its current mux.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the core's combinational MUL/MULH/MULHU/MULHSU execution with
one two-stage multiplier spanning the existing EX and MEM stages.
Keep IF -> ID -> OF -> EX -> MEM -> WB, single issue, nret=1, and the
current six-RUN-clock divider. This is a structural movement of the
multiplier's register boundary, not a predictor or memory change.

In EX, split each registered source into low and high sixteen-bit
limbs. Encode each limb as a signed seventeen-bit value: low limbs
have a zero sign bit; a high limb has its source's bit 31 as the extra
sign bit only when that operand is signed for the selected multiply
opcode. MUL and MULHU use unsigned limbs, MULH signs both high limbs,
and MULHSU signs only rs1's high limb. Compute four independent native
17x17 products and register them at EX/MEM, with the instruction's
ordinary control, PC, rd, source values and RVFI metadata. Explicitly
size products to thirty-four signed bits. No product addition,
completed-product selection or multiply-result forwarding belongs
before these registers. Infer DSP multiplication with portable RTL;
do not require vendor primitives or alter synthesis scripts.

In MEM reconstruct the sixty-four-bit product modulo 2^64 as
P00 + (sign_extend(P01) << 16) + (sign_extend(P10) << 16)
    + (sign_extend(P11) << 32).
Extend each signed partial before shifting. P00's low sixteen bits
can bypass reduction; all other terms are zero below bit sixteen.
Combine the remaining forty-eight-bit terms with two explicit
carry-save compressors and one final carry-propagate addition,
rather than a chain of three wide '+' operators. Select the low
thirty-two bits for MUL and the high thirty-two bits for the other
three operations. Signed limb decomposition supplies signed high
results directly, without serial full-width sign-correction subtracts.
Capture this value in the existing MEM/WB result field and expose the
same value to the ordinary MEM-to-OF forwarding path. A nonmultiply
continues using its existing EX/MEM ALU result and memory extraction.
Keep dmem addresses/enables driven from the current registered memory
payload, with no multiplier reduction in any memory-request path.

Remove real multiply networks from the core's combinational ALU
elaboration using a constant parameter. Preserve its default standalone
combinational interface and all existing arithmetic tests. In the
pipelined core's RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS build capture the exact existing
multiply stand-in at EX/MEM, and publish it from MEM with identical
producer availability, interlocks and retirement timing to real RTL.
Preserve all four ALTOPS constants and operand formulas exactly.

Treat a valid legal EX multiply with nonzero rd as an unavailable EX
producer, like an EX load. If the valid OF instruction actually uses
that rd, hold ID/OF and decode consumption, invalidate the next OF/EX
word, and let the multiply advance once into MEM. At the next accepting
edge resolve the consumer from the completed MEM product. Independent
instructions, including independent multiplies, advance every clock;
this is not a globally blocking multicycle multiply unit. The youngest
writer must win over older MEM/WB values even while its result is
unavailable. Use decoded use_rs1/use_rs2 flags so immediate fields,
unused raw RVFI source fields and x0 cannot add functional interlocks.
Preserve verification-only correction of unused source fields from
completed MEM and WB values. Extend EX/OF unit tests to require the
new producer schedule without weakening source/result assertions.

dmem stalls hold the entire EX/MEM partial-product payload and younger
stages; retained WB provenance remains valid. Division wait drains an
older MEM multiply once without replaying it. Redirects discard every
younger valid word before memory, RF or predictor side effects; a
wrong-path multiply cannot retire. Preserve reset cancellation,
current branch training/recovery, alignment traps, default-illegal
decoding, EBREAK-only SYSTEM legality, exact RVFI operands and rd
results, +1 order, all bus handshakes, and the unchanged ten-clock
symbolic-progress bound. Do not modify any evaluation contract.

The expected gain is a frequency increase large enough to outweigh
one extra clock per immediate multiply dependency. This is an
unmeasured forecast. At unchanged cycles acceptance requires fitness
above 182.92448 iterations/second, approximately 73.62 MHz; with a
three-percent cycle cost it requires approximately 75.83 MHz.
The unchanged divider and MEM reduction/forwarding may become the
next limits. Require actual median Gowin Fmax times canonical
marker-bracketed CoreMark iterations/cycle, all CRC/UART/bounds checks,
exact multiply arithmetic tests and every unchanged formal/cosim gate.

title: Predecode branch prediction verification polarity at the operand boundary
motivation:
The champion achieves 174.88 iter/sec at median 70.381 MHz and 4,024,573 marker-bracketed CoreMark cycles. LESSONS.md is absent. Prior target, loop, return-shadow and tagged-history supplements saved few cycles and lost frequency; delayed training and registered squash also regressed. A fresh unchanged-parent Gowin option-0 run reproduces 69.480 MHz and the reported 19.498 ns worst path: OF/EX operand flop, ordering comparator, train_taken selection, recovery control, OF operand mux, multiplier input register. Comparator output has fanout 194. Divider feedback paths are almost tied, so increasing predictor complexity is particularly risky.

Local scratch checks of narrower operand kills, payload-enable splits, deferred training/squash and smaller predictor tables did not beat the champion. This motivates retaining its exact predictor behavior and immediate recovery while shortening verification itself. Current direction verification selects and possibly complements the actual branch condition, then XORs the captured prediction. The condition's true/complement polarity and predicted direction are both known before EX and need not be combined after operand comparison.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one branch_recovery_invert bit to OF/EX, computed at the existing accepting operand edge as in.ctrl.branch_op[0] XOR in.predicted_taken. All six legal branch encodings use funct3 bit zero for relation inversion: BEQ/BLT/BLTU use the base comparison, while BNE/BGE/BGEU use its complement. Thus a direction mismatch can be computed in EX by applying the already registered combined polarity directly to the base operand comparison.

Retain the existing actual branch_cond computation for architectural branch_taken, RVFI pc_next and counter training. Compute branch_pred_wrong separately: BEQ/BNE use (rs1 == rs2) XOR branch_recovery_invert; BLT/BGE use signed (rs1 < rs2) XOR that bit; BLTU/BGEU use unsigned (rs1 < rs2) XOR that bit; default remains zero. Express the inversion inside each relation arm so the late comparison does not first pass through the actual-condition output and its branch-operation polarity selection. The synthesis tool may share base comparators, but recovery must consume this direct verification result rather than branch_cond XOR predicted_taken. Do not rewrite the existing comparators into a different arithmetic engine.

Preserve the exact misalignment convention. Conditional mismatch is misalign_fault ? in.predicted_taken : branch_pred_wrong, inside the existing accepted, legal conditional-branch qualification. This is algebraically equivalent to effective_taken XOR predicted_taken, including a taken branch whose target traps. Keep the current valid/nonstalled/nondivide EX acceptance gate and aligned JALR redirect. The original predicted_taken bit still selects the conditional recovery address: predicted taken selects PC+4, predicted not taken selects the branch target. Retain exact JAL prediction, JALR target calculation and bit-zero clearing, actual RVFI next PCs, link-write suppression on traps, and unchanged recovery latency.

Capture the new polarity atomically with operands, PC, controls and prediction under the existing OF acceptance condition. Preserve it on OF/EX holds; reset clears it with the bundle. A flush kills validity exactly as today, and an invalid payload's polarity cannot authorize recovery or any other side effect. Add no new field to fetch entries, IF/ID or ID/OF: their existing decoded branch_op and captured predicted_taken already provide the inputs. EX/MEM and MEM/WB need no polarity field because recovery completes in EX. No stage, prediction table, speculative history, training delay, target cache or deferred squash is introduced.

Keep the folded-PC 64x2 table, local Boolean saturation, weakly-taken initialization, raw legal/aligned predecode, old-state updates and exact accepted training events unchanged. Preserve the EX-only divider, integer/multiply forwarding, load-use interlock, queue behavior, bus handshakes, held-WB provenance, decoder legality, alignment traps, nret=1 ports, strict retirement order, symbolic progress and every eval invariant.

The intended gain is higher frequency at exactly unchanged dynamic instruction and cycle counts; six percent is a low-confidence projection, not an observed result. Divider feedback and placement may prevent a gain even if verification loses a logic level. At unchanged 4,024,573 cycles, acceptance requires median Gowin Fmax above approximately 73.62 MHz and fitness above 182.92448. Validate both directions of every branch type under arbitrary predictions, signed/unsigned extreme operands, misalignment, loads and divisions, plus reset and independent bus stalls. Keep all formal/cosim checks, canonical CRC/UART validation, memory bounds and marker-bracketed scoring unchanged. Evaluate every scored placement option; do not claim acceptance from an option-0 result alone.

title: Balanced nibble comparison shortens the EX branch recovery path
motivation:
The champion scores 174.88 iter/sec at 70.381 MHz with 4,024,573
marker-bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its reported worst path starts at
an OF/EX operand register, passes through EX branch ordering comparison
and recovery control into OF, and ends at a multiplier input register;

radix-16 expansion, direct one-hot forwarding, multiplier pipelining,
and predecoded prediction polarity. The latter retained the original
full-width comparisons. A local replacement of the comparison network
therefore addresses an untried source of dependent arithmetic depth

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace only EX's branch operand comparison with a combinational,
explicitly balanced lexicographic comparison tree. Divide each 32-bit
operand into eight four-bit unsigned slices. For slice i compute
E_i = (a_i == b_i) and L_i = (a_i < b_i) independently. Combine a more
significant group H and a less significant group L with
E = E_H & E_L and LT = LT_H | (E_H & LT_L). Build three explicit levels

halfwords, and two halfwords to one word. Do not use a serial loop
recurrence or replace the final tree with a full-width less-than
expression. Equality is the root E, unsigned ordering is the root LT,
and signed ordering is (a[31] ^ b[31]) ? a[31] : LT. This shares one
unsigned ordering tree across both signed and unsigned branches and

group selection targets Gowin LUT4 mapping rather than a 32-bit carry
propagation path into the high-fanout branch recovery control.

title: Early load execution behind a registered effective-address boundary
motivation:
The champion scores 174.88 iterations/second at median 70.381 MHz and
4,024,573 marker-bracketed CoreMark cycles. LESSONS.md is absent. The
structural history shows that registering resolved operands and launching
division exclusively from EX improved frequency substantially. The recent
partial-product multiplier lost frequency and exposed divider timing.
Earlier MEM-to-executing-EX load forwarding saved cycles but connected
live memory data to arithmetic and recovery paths, limiting its benefit.

The current six-stage pipeline still inserts one bubble whenever an EX
load produces an actual source of the OF instruction. This remains true
with a ready memory bus. Moving the load request one stage earlier,
behind a registered effective address, can deliver its result to the
existing OF operand flops on that same accepting edge. The consumer's
execution remains isolated from the live bus. Scratch timing probes of
branch-comparison retiming, wider fetch buffering and removal of the ID
register did not beat this champion; an additional register or a deeper
queue alone is not a sufficient structural improvement.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Retiming only load execution should reduce dependent-load bubbles while
preserving the resolved operand boundary: compute a legal load's effective
address during OF, register it atomically with the OF/EX instruction and
operands, issue that load from EX, and capture both the memory response
and the consuming OF instruction's resolved operands at the successful
handshake edge. Keep IF -> ID -> OF -> EX -> MEM -> WB, single issue,
nret=1, the existing predictor and fetch queue, and the exact multiplier
and six-RUN-clock divider. This is one structural change in load stage
placement and result availability, with the existing external memory bus.

Add a registered early_load_addr to OF/EX. Its value is the final
x0-corrected, age-prioritized rs1 operand plus the decoded immediate,
modulo 32 bits. Compute the sum only on the load path; ordinary integer,
branch, store and multiply execution keep their present operands and
stage placement. Preserve the accepting-edge payload enable and holds.
EX loads use this address register directly, including its low bits for
alignment and byte extraction; they do not recompute the address through
the EX ALU. The new address path must never run through a current EX
arithmetic result, completed divider result, or live early-load response
before another wide addition in the same clock.

Enforce that last constraint with a selective address dependency
interlock: when a valid legal OF load actually uses a nonzero rs1 that
matches the youngest accepted EX register writer, hold ID/OF and decode
consumption and insert an OF/EX bubble while that writer advances once.
On the next accepting edge form the load address from its registered MEM
result, then WB/RF as appropriate. Include completed division and accepted
early loads in this producer classification. An older matching MEM/WB
writer must not satisfy the dependency while the youngest EX writer is
unavailable. This interlock is limited to load address generation; other
consumers may capture the accepted early-load result without a bubble.
Existing decoded source-use flags, legality, writer qualification and x0
rules remain mandatory. Keep division launch exclusively from OF/EX.

Use the single dmem port in program order. An outstanding legal aligned
MEM store owns it ahead of an EX load, including on the store's successful
handshake clock: never perform two memory operations on one edge. While
that store stalls, preserve its complete address/data/mask request. On
its accepting edge retire/drain it normally, insert an EX/MEM bubble and
hold the younger EX load; issue the load on the following cycle. Stores
retain their MEM stage. Consecutive accepted EX loads may issue every
clock because a load entering MEM already owns a captured response and
must not request the bus again. FENCE behavior remains ordered by this
in-order execution and completion protocol.

An eligible EX load asserts read enable using its registered address only
when no older store owns the bus. Gate illegal and misaligned requests
off. If io_dmemReady is low, hold the EX load, its address and both younger
payload stages; keep the read request stable. Older non-memory MEM/WB
instructions drain once rather than being replayed. Distinguish holding
an outstanding MEM store from holding the executing early load: do not
freeze a drainable EX/MEM instruction just because the younger EX load is
waiting, and do not overwrite a stalled store with a bubble. These are
independent ownership/advance conditions, not a global hold of every
backend register. Reset cancels ownership and pending valid state.

On an accepted aligned EX load, format the live bus word with that load's
registered width, signedness and address offset. Expose the resulting
architectural value as a youngest EX forwarding producer only while
request-valid and io_dmemReady are true. Capture it in OF/EX for an
immediate ALU, branch/JALR, store-data/store-address, multiply or divide
consumer; none of those execution units may consume live dmem directly.
A load that generates the next load's address uses the selective bubble
described above. Qualify every consumer transfer with successful older
memory acceptance; bus stalls never authorize speculative captures,
branch training, redirect or divider launch.

Capture the early load's raw memory word, formatted value, effective
address and exact instruction/RVFI payload into EX/MEM at that same edge.
MEM uses the captured response for WB and for its registered-result bypass;
it must not resample io_dmemRData or emit a second read. Keep rd_wdata equal
to the captured sign/zero-extended value; RVFI mem_rdata reports the raw
accepted word, mem_addr is word-aligned and mem_rmask describes the byte
lanes. A misaligned load retires once with a trap, no memory request and
no RF/forwarding write, without waiting for an irrelevant bus-ready bit.
WB remains the architectural RF write and single-channel retirement
boundary. Preserve retained WB forwarding provenance while other stages
are held, exact source metadata and strict +1 retirement order.

Preserve all decoder default-illegal and EBREAK-only SYSTEM checks,
branch/jump alignment and recovery behavior, memory bounds and MMIO
ordering, all real and ALTOPS arithmetic formulas, outstanding-request
stability, wrong-path suppression and the unchanged ten-cycle symbolic
progress bound. No early request may come from an OF instruction that an
accepted older EX redirect is killing. A request begins only from the
registered valid EX load. No contract files or nret changes are included.

The forecast is an eight-percent fitness improvement, with low confidence;
this early-load circuit has not been implemented or measured. The new
OF address adder, dmem ownership mux and store-to-load serialization are
material costs, and the unchanged divider can still limit Fmax. The
selective load-address interlock trades some cycle savings for keeping
current EX arithmetic and live load data out of the address adder. Do not
assume that every current load-use bubble disappears or infer a gain from
an IPC result alone. Acceptance requires fitness above 182.92448 iter/sec.
For a five-percent reduction from the champion's bracketed cycle count,
median Gowin Fmax must exceed approximately 69.94 MHz; at unchanged cycles
it must exceed approximately 73.62 MHz. Measure canonical CoreMark cycles
between the MMIO markers, validate all five CRCs and the UART literal,
and run every unchanged formal/cosim gate and scored placement option.

title: Prevalidate direct targets for conditional prediction verification
motivation:
The champion scores 174.88 iter/sec at 70.381 MHz and 4,024,573 timed
CoreMark cycles. LESSONS.md is absent. Tagged target, loop-exit,
return-shadow and history supplements saved few cycles and lost Fmax;
delayed training, delayed squash and registered verification polarity
also regressed. A fresh unchanged-parent Gowin option-0 run reproduces
69.480 MHz and the 19.498 ns EX-comparator-to-OF path, including a
branch-condition node with fanout 194. Local comparator retiming and
shared-comparator experiments did not clear the acceptance margin.

Current verification incorporates misalign_fault, which itself includes
the actual branch condition. For an unaligned direct target the effective
taken direction is always zero, whether the branch is untaken or taken
and trapping. Direct-target alignment depends only on PC and immediate,
both known before EX. Carrying that fact across OF/EX allows verification
to qualify the prediction directly without rebuilding alignment through
the late operand-dependent trap predicate.

capture edge compute target_low = (in.pc[1:0] + in.imm[1:0]) modulo four

conditional branch compute prediction mismatch as

an aligned target uses the actual direction, while an unaligned target

accept and !flush in every wide payload capture enable; both depend on
the late EX redirect. Thus resolving an older branch controls whether

accept && in.valid && !stall && !flush to in.valid && !stall. Keep the
existing valid update exactly: reset clears the bundle, flush clears
reg_q.valid with priority over stall, and an unstalled cycle assigns

qualify a forwarding writer, issue a memory access, write the RF or
retire. EX already qualifies these actions with instruction validity;
retain and verify those qualifications. A flush while stalled must
still clear only valid and retain the complete payload. During load-use,
divide and dmem holds, all payload fields remain held exactly as today.
Every surviving accepted instruction captures the same resolved source
values and metadata on the same edge as before. An unstalled accept=0
can update an invalid payload but cannot authorize any instruction.

memory backpressure, retained WB forwarding provenance, all alignment
traps, decoder default-illegal and EBREAK-only SYSTEM behavior, nret=1

title: Spatial divider stages with local divisor banks remove shared feedback and fanout
motivation:
The champion scores 174.88 iter/sec at 70.381 MHz in 4,024,573 timed
CoreMark cycles. LESSONS.md is absent. The structural history repeatedly
improves by shortening division; r4s1 still reused one physical digit
chain, whereas this proposal removes that reuse. Recent multiplier
pipelining and early load execution regressed. The latest neighboring
attempts also expose the shared divider as the limiting path. Local
scratch separation of operand-payload enables did not establish a gain;
removing launch qualification from divider payload capture measured only
64.099 MHz median. The remaining opportunity is to remove the feedback
and bootstrap/body selection network, rather than further tune it.
