hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace only the reused full-width divider body with five physically
distinct registered prefix stages and local registered divisor banks. Preserve the accepted EX-only launch,
existing four-bit launch computation, six-bit narrow bootstrap, six RUN
clocks, terminal two-bit publication and start/busy/result-valid/consume
interface. This is a spatial unrolling and width specialization of the
existing divider, not an additional CPU instruction stage or a faster
formal-only implementation.

At launch L retain the magnitude suffix, four-bit quotient/remainder,
full unsigned divisor, signedness flags and captured narrow multiples.
At L+1 run the existing six-bit bootstrap once, register the resulting
ten-bit remainder and quotient state, and prepare full-width 3D from
registered D as today. Hold those bootstrap registers afterward; they
must no longer be overwritten by the recurring body.

At L+2, L+3, L+4, L+5 and L+6 advance into separate body registers after
14, 18, 22, 26 and 30 processed dividend bits respectively. Each stage
contains two radix-4 trial/subtract/select cells. Its first cell has an
N-2-bit window and its second an N-bit window, where N is that stage's
processed-bit count. Inputs come only from the preceding stage's flops,
never a mux over feedback and bootstrap results. Use statically sized
remainder fields: 10 bits after bootstrap, then 14/18/22/26/30 bits.
Quotient storage may remain 32 bits initially; explicitly size arithmetic
and trim dead quotient storage where synthesis does not already do so.
No stage may recompute the preceding stage combinationally.

A prefix after p dividend bits is below 2^p, including when D=0, so its
trial window and restored remainder need only p bits. For a p-bit trial
window T, trial multiple M in {D,2D,3D} is eligible only when all full
34-bit multiple bits above p-1 are zero. Compute diff as the p+1-bit
zero-extended subtraction of T and M[p-1:0]; ok is eligibility AND no
borrow. Preserve the exact full multiples and explicit upper-bit check:
truncating a large divisor or multiple without this check is incorrect.
Use the current quotient-digit equations and disjoint masked-OR remainder
selection. Keep native subtraction/carry inference; do not substitute
custom carry-lookahead arithmetic or a priority comparator/subtractor.

Retain full D and 3D as the operation's setup state, but do not drive
all body trial banks directly from these stationary high-fanout flops.
For each p=N stage capture local low-N-bit D/2D/3D banks and the six
full-multiple eligibility flags needed by its N-2 and N-bit cells on the
preceding phase's edge. Thus the 14-bit bank captures at bootstrap L+1;
the 18/22/26/30-bit banks capture at L+2/L+3/L+4/L+5 respectively, before
their consumers run. Each bank has a different phase enable and holds
its operands throughout its consuming stage. This temporal distinction
must survive synthesis; do not use identical same-edge copies that the
tool can merge. Body trial subtraction and digit selection read only
the matching local multiple flops and registered eligibility flags.
The arithmetic borrow must still be combined with its saved eligibility.

For the first body bank at L+1, form full 3D from registered D and use
that same exact widened expression to capture its truncated local 3D
and both eligibility flags; do not read the old global 3D flop on that
edge. Later local banks capture the already registered full 3D. Keep
setup capture independent of preceding body arithmetic and digit
selection. Earlier local banks may hold values from a previous operation
until their scheduled capture, but no valid stage may use those stale
values. Reset clears bank state; each accepted operation overwrites
every bank before use. Only one division is active, so captured setup
state cannot be replaced until consume or consume/relaunch.

Capture each remainder/quotient stage once on its matching RUN phase,
and hold the final thirty-bit state throughout READY. No completed-state
phase-indexed wide mux is permitted. The existing terminal bank reads
the final stage directly and retains full D/2D/3D for the last two-bit
trials and parallel signed-result candidates, without another clock.
Enter READY after L+6 and consume at L+7 when EX/MEM accepts, exactly
as the champion. On consume/relaunch the consumer observes the old
completed result before new launch state takes effect.

Reset cancels every valid phase. Reject starts while busy and retain
READY output until consume. Preserve divide-by-zero, INT_MIN/-1, signed
remainder rules and the exact ALTOPS formulas with the identical six-RUN
schedule. Preserve EX operand correctness, RVFI metadata, division ownership,
branch recovery latency, forwarding priority, load-use bubbles, held-WB
provenance, memory handshakes and nret=1 top-level IO. Consecutive divides retain
the eight-cycle retirement gap; redirect-to-divide retains the unchanged
ten-cycle progress bound. No evaluation file or correctness check changes.

This is one structural divider change: a feedforward chain of distinct
prefix stages with local registered arithmetic operands replaces shared
recurring state, feedback selection and stationary divisor fanout.
Leave OF capture, accepted EX producer qualification, branch recovery,
prediction, memory execution and multiplication exactly as in the parent.

A scratch spatial prototype using stationary shared multiples measured
67.274/71.000/71.000 MHz, 5,298 LUT4s and 1,245 FFs. It passed all 31
pipeline tests, eight EX tests and the real-divider arithmetic suite;
canonical stalled CoreMark retained exactly 4,024,573 marker-bracketed
cycles, all five CRCs, the validation literal and no out-of-bounds access.
Its approximately 0.88% fitness gain is below acceptance. Local operand
and eligibility banks are therefore essential to this final proposal;
the final banked circuit is unmeasured, and no acceptance is claimed.
A separate capture-control variant regressed and is excluded.

An eight-percent fitness improvement is a low-confidence forecast; extra
routing, local-bank setup paths and the unchanged EX-to-OF path may
limit the benefit. Require the final median Gowin Fmax times canonical
marker-bracketed iterations/cycle above 182.92448 iter/sec, approximately
73.62 MHz at unchanged cycles. Validate all real/ALTOPS divider tests,
pipeline tests, unchanged formal/cosim gates, every CRC, UART literal,
memory bounds and all scored placement options.

title: ID predecode registers one-hot conditions for prediction recovery
motivation:
The champion scores 174.88 iter/sec at 70.381 MHz with 4,024,573 timed CoreMark cycles. LESSONS.md is absent. Prior tagged-target, loop, return-shadow and history supplements saved less than one percent of cycles and lost Fmax; delayed training/squash, scalar recovery polarity and static target prevalidation also regressed. An unchanged-parent scratch Gowin run reproduces 69.480 MHz on option zero and its 19.498 ns comparator-to-OF path. Local payload-enable separation, counter re-encoding and operand-comparison summaries also lost frequency.

A scratch prototype that registers complete one-hot prediction-failure conditions at OF/EX measures options 0/1/2 = 69.118/70.190/70.190 MHz, versus the champion's 70.381 MHz median. It retains exactly 4,024,573 cycles and passes warning-free lint, selftest and all three random-program RVFI cosims with and without stalls, canonical CoreMark CRC/UART validation and memory bounds. This is close to the parent but does not clear acceptance. Moving the same predecode into ID removes its class/polarity/alignment logic from the OF register input and acceptance cone, while retaining immediate EX recovery. It is a distinct complete one-hot verification predecode, rather than another scalar polarity or alignment-only change.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a seven-bit recovery_mode to id_of_t and id_ex_t, before instr in each bundle so the existing instr/predicted_taken/valid tail stays intact. Compute recovery_mode in ID from the validated decoded branch_op, fetched prediction and exact PC-plus-B-immediate alignment; do not compare operands in ID or OF. Let aligned mean the low-two-bit PC-plus-immediate sum is zero, and invert = branch_op[0] XOR predicted_taken. For an aligned target select exactly one condition: BEQ/BNE select bit 0 for equal if invert=0 or bit 1 for unequal if invert=1; BLT/BGE select bit 2 for signed-less or bit 3 for signed-greater-or-equal; BLTU/BGEU select bit 4 for unsigned-less or bit 5 for unsigned-greater-or-equal. Other comparison arms are zero. Bit 6 is !aligned && predicted_taken. Reserved comparison classes select no relation. This seventh bit preserves verification even for inconsistent prediction metadata: an unaligned direct target has effective direction zero.

Register this mode with its instruction in ID/OF under the existing payload !stall rule. OF only copies the matching mode into OF/EX at its existing accepted operand edge. Reset clears it with each bundle; holds preserve it, and flush kills validity exactly as today. Retain the original prediction bit for choosing the conditional recovery address. No IF/ID or queue metadata, stage, speculative history or deferred squash is added. The final extra state is fourteen bits, seven at each existing register boundary.

In EX form recovery_wrong as a balanced OR of the six masked ordinary full-width operand relations and bit 6. Consume these registered masks directly, bypassing actual branch_cond selection, branch-operation inversion, predicted-direction XOR and misalign_fault in conditional verification. Keep the existing outer ex_accept && !is_illegal && is_branch qualification and unchanged aligned JALR recovery arm. Do not move acceptance, qualify producer eligibility differently or alter wide payload enables. For aligned legal branches this equals branch_cond XOR predicted_taken; for an unaligned direct target it equals predicted_taken. The actual branch_cond case remains unchanged for architectural taken status, trap checks, actual RVFI pc_next and accepted table training. JAL/JALR targets, bit-zero clearing, PC+4 links and trapping-link suppression remain exact.

Retain immediate prediction-selected correction addresses, same-edge queue discard and both younger-stage validity kills. Keep the folded-PC 64x2 bimodal table, local Boolean saturation, weakly-taken reset, raw aligned/legal BRANCH/JAL predecode, old-state lookup and every existing training event. Preserve arithmetic, EX-only divider launch/consume, forwarding, load-use bubbles, all bus acceptance/hold rules, WB provenance, decoder legality, nret=1 ports, strict RVFI order, symbolic progress and every evaluation invariant. This is one predictor-verification retiming hypothesis.

The intended gain is frequency with identical predictions, recovery latency and benchmark cycles. Six percent is a low-confidence forecast for the final ID-predecoded design, not an observed improvement from the OF prototype. The unchanged divider and placement may prevent any gain. Acceptance at unchanged cycles requires median Gowin Fmax above approximately 73.62 MHz and fitness above 182.92448 iter/sec. motivation: The champion scores 174.88 iter/sec at 70.381 MHz with 4,024,573 marker-bracketed CoreMark cycles. LESSONS.md is absent. hypothesis.hypothesis:
Predecode the ALU result selector once in ID and carry nineteen one-hot operation masks through the existing ID/OF and OF/EX bundles. Define mask bit k to select ALU operation value k, for the existing ALU_ADD=0 through ALU_REMU=18 constants. ID computes this mask from the already validated decoder's dec_alu_op and registers it with the same instruction under the existing payload !stall rule. Invalid or illegal words may carry the decoder's default ADD mask but retain their original validity and default-illegal control; a mask never authorizes retirement, a producer or a side effect. Preserve the scalar alu_op field for divider operation/sign decoding, ALTOPS operation discrimination and every existing control gate. Do not recode the architectural decoder or replace its default-illegal rules.

Add the mask before the existing ctrl/instr/prediction/valid tail in id_of_t and id_ex_t, so those established low-order fields keep their bit offsets. OF only copies the matching ID/OF mask at its unchanged accepted operand-capture edge; no opcode decode or comparator is added to OF. Reset clears mask state with each existing bundle, holds retain it and validity kills retain their existing priority. Exactly thirty-eight extra selector bits are carried across two existing boundaries; no new stage, skid entry, architectural latency or additional interlock is introduced.

Extend alu.sv with a default-false USE_PREDECODED_SELECT parameter and a nineteen-bit select input. Default standalone instances derive equivalent masks locally from scalar op, retaining their current public combinational behavior. In the core set USE_PREDECODED_SELECT=true and connect the registered OF/EX masks from ex_stage. For this mode use each mask directly as the enable of its existing 32-bit arithmetic result and combine terms with an explicitly balanced masked-OR tree. Do not feed the scalar opcode back into the final result mux. ADD/SUB, logic, signed/unsigned comparisons, three shifts, LUI, the three existing native products and the divide-result path retain their current arithmetic and signedness; do not consolidate products, add partial-product compressors, alter barrel-shifter structure or change division. MUL reads the existing unsigned low product, and MULH/MULHU/MULHSU select the existing exact high products. For each of the four divide/rem selectors use the existing div_result. In ALTOPS builds keep every existing formula and constant exact, and gate its result with the corresponding mask. A zero mask produces zero, and all legal decoded instructions carry exactly one mask. Keep COMBINATIONAL_DIV and SEPARATE_MUL_OPERANDS behavior unchanged.

This is one local decode-retiming optimization: operation-result qualification is registered before EX instead of decoding the five-bit opcode after OF/EX. The final reduction must be balanced, not a procedural priority chain, and no broad one-hot rewrite of forwarding, branch recovery, producer acceptance or payload enables is included. Keep the parent pipeline's EX-only divider launch, six-RUN real/ALTOPS schedule, normal/divide producer timing, load bubbles, retained WB provenance, all memory handshakes, prediction/training/recovery and alignment traps. Preserve nret=1 top-level IO, strictly increasing RVFI order, exact source/result/PC/memory fields, EBREAK-only SYSTEM legality, symbolic progress and every evaluation/correctness gate.

An eight-percent fitness gain is a low-confidence forecast for this final, unmeasured circuit. At identical cycles acceptance requires median Gowin Fmax above approximately 73.62 MHz and fitness above 182.92448 iter/sec. marker-bracketed CoreMark cycles. LESSONS.md is absent. Structural
history improved operand registration and divider scheduling, but
multiplier pipelining, early loads and spatial divider stages regressed.
No prior structural attempt introduced a committed store queue. The
current hazard unit freezes EX/MEM and every younger stage whenever
any MEM load or store sees io_dmemReady=0. Ordinary RAM stores need no
returned value, yet approximately 22 percent bus backpressure stops
arithmetic, operand capture and decode. A small queue can separate
architectural store commitment from physical bus service.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a two-entry FIFO of committed ordinary-RAM stores behind MEM.
An aligned legal store to [0x00000000,0x00100000) completes its MEM
pipeline transfer when either the external bus accepts it directly or
the FIFO accepts its address, replicated write data and four-bit mask.
Its normal MEM/WB payload then retires exactly once on channel 0,
even if io_dmemReady was low at enqueue. The FIFO owns the irrevocable
write until bus acknowledgment. This is one structural change to MEM
completion and pipeline backpressure. Keep the six stages and nret=1.

For an empty queue retain direct-store fall-through: drive the current
MEM store on the bus and, if ready, advance without saving a duplicate.
If not ready, enqueue the same request and advance the pipeline. Its
address/data/mask must remain identical as ownership moves from EX/MEM
to the queue. With queued entries, the oldest alone owns the write bus
and pops only on io_dmemReady. A younger RAM store may enqueue on that
same edge; a full queue accepts a replacement when its head dequeues.
Preserve FIFO order and every store; do not merge stores. Drain queued
requests during normal execution, divider waits, imem stalls and
front-end holds. Redirects never discard committed entries.

Loads remain blocking and issue only when the store FIFO is empty.
Do not add alias comparison or store-to-load forwarding. After an older
queued store drains on an edge, a held load may begin the next cycle.
Every accepted load therefore includes every older architectural store,
including overlapping byte and halfword writes. Preserve extraction,
alignment traps, load-use bubbles and accepted MEM-to-OF forwarding.
A load waiting behind stores must not expose the queue head's address
or data as its RVFI access or become a premature forwarding producer.

Every access outside ordinary RAM follows the existing serialized
direct path after the FIFO drains. UART and both benchmark marker
stores MUST wait for external bus acknowledgment before advancing
MEM or retiring. Never enqueue MMIO or alias a high address to RAM.
Start is acknowledged after preceding stores; stop is acknowledged
after all benchmark stores. The scored timing window must include
outstanding benchmark writes. EBREAK and accepted MISC-MEM/FENCE
instructions also wait for an empty FIFO, so termination and fences
cannot abandon committed writes. Preserve current decoder legality.

Export actual MEM-blocked from instruction completion rules: ordinary
store capacity, load/MMIO queue draining and bus readiness, or a
fence/EBREAK drain barrier. Replace the blanket memory-op&&!ready
freeze with this signal. A pending FIFO write alone does not hold a
nonmemory instruction. When MEM really blocks, preserve EX/MEM and
younger-stage holds, MEM/WB valid clearing and retained-WB forwarding
provenance. Otherwise MEM/WB captures the current pipeline instruction
once, never the bus owner's previously committed instruction. Divider
launch/consume and accepted redirects respect actual older MEM blocking.

Separate architectural MEM payload from physical bus ownership. At
enqueue, RVFI carries that store's original PC, sources, aligned
address, mask and replicated data through the existing retirement
boundary. Dequeue produces no retirement and never increments order.
At a direct load, RVFI captures its accepted read word. Physical dmem
outputs select the oldest queued store or the direct request; read and
write ownership are mutually exclusive. Hold requests stable while
io_dmemReady=0. Resolve coincident direct acceptance, enqueue and dequeue
explicitly to prevent duplicate writes. Only valid, legal, aligned
current MEM stores enqueue; wrong-path or trapping stores never do.

Reset clears FIFO occupancy and cancels requests as it resets the
existing pipeline. Preserve exact +1 retirement order and source values,
real/ALTOPS arithmetic and availability, decoder default-illegal and
EBREAK-only SYSTEM rules, memory bounds, branch recovery and unchanged
symbolic liveness checks. Under ready-bus symbolic streams sustain
one store per clock through direct service or simultaneous pop/enqueue;
draining must not add an unbounded phase. Change no contract file.

Forecast eight percent greater fitness with low confidence. Fewer
global store-stall cycles must compensate for FIFO and arbitration
timing costs; loads after stores still serialize. The final store-queue
circuit is unimplemented and unmeasured. Alternative divider-lane and
forwarding-topology scratch probes did not clear acceptance and are
excluded; no measured gain is claimed for this proposal. Require
actual median Gowin Fmax times canonical bracketed iterations/cycle
above 182.92448 iter/sec. At unchanged Fmax that requires more than
4.4 percent fewer cycles; with six percent fewer cycles the required
Fmax is approximately 69.20 MHz. Validate every unchanged formal/cosim
gate, canonical CRCs, UART validation literal, memory bounds and marker
drain ordering before judging the scored placements.

title: Reuse EX/MEM payloads for registered predictor correction and training
motivation:
The champion scores 174.88 iter/sec at 70.381 MHz with 4,024,573 timed
CoreMark cycles. LESSONS.md is absent. Prior target, loop, link-shadow
and history supplements saved less than one percent of cycles and lost
frequency. Delayed training, immediate-PC/delayed-squash recovery,
polarity predecode, target-alignment prevalidation and one-hot recovery
predecode also regressed. The recorded parent timing investigation
identifies a near-critical EX operand-comparator-to-OF capture path,
including a branch-condition node with fanout 194. Adding predictor
capacity is therefore less promising than removing live verification
from all frontend controls, including the fetch-PC input.

Registering complete correction ordinarily adds a recovery cycle and
can violate the unchanged ten-cycle progress check on branch-to-DIV
traces. A registered-target fetch bypass can supply the corrected
instruction on the original target-decode edge, avoiding that penalty.
This differs from prior registered-squash attempts, which retained a
live EX-comparator connection to the ordinary fetch-PC register.

A scratch protocol prototype with a separate 32-bit recovery-target
register passes all 53 unchanged fast formal checks, eight full-RVFI
selftest/random-program cosims with and without bus stalls, and the
canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/bounds checks at exactly 4,024,573 cycles.
Its 66.894 MHz median regresses, and variants that change capture
enables also do not clear acceptance. Target-only payload reuse reaches
67.460 MHz and also regresses. The final proposal therefore reuses
EX/MEM payloads for both correction targets and training context,
eliminating the separate target and training-payload registers. The
protocol checks support correctness and latency. The final complete
payload-reuse prototype's separate measurements are recorded below.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Retain the existing folded-PC 64x2 bimodal predictor and direct JAL
prediction. Replace the live EX redirect feedback with one registered
correction transaction: correction_valid_q and a full 32-bit recovery
target carried in the existing EX/MEM write_data field. At each accepted,
valid, legal EX control transfer,
capture the existing conditional direction-mismatch or aligned JALR
correction decision. Select a conditional recovery target from the
instruction's saved predicted_taken bit, independently of its actual
operand comparison: predicted taken selects PC+4, otherwise PC+imm.
JALR uses its exact resolved target with bit zero cleared. For decoded
branches or JALR, next_payload.write_data is that preselected recovery
target; every other instruction retains the original raw rs2 store
data. Neither branch nor JALR can assert mem_write, so this reuses an
existing 32-bit timed register without altering any actual store.
Do not reuse alu_result: JALR still needs its architectural PC+4 link.
The independent rs2_val field continues carrying exact RVFI source
data. Register correction_valid_q on the same EX/MEM accepting edge,
and read correction_target as ex_mem_w.write_data only when that valid
bit is set. No separate target register or target-write enable exists.
correction_valid_q becomes zero on every no-event edge; reset clears
it and the ordinary EX/MEM bundle. Retain current trap conventions and
accepted-EX qualification exactly. Target selection depends on decoded
class and saved prediction, never the late conditional comparator.

Register conditional-table training validity at the same acceptance
boundary. For a decoded conditional branch, replace the otherwise
architecturally unused EX/MEM alu_result with
{26'd0, in.pc[7:2] XOR in.pc[13:8]}. These instructions have reg_write,
mem_read and mem_write all zero. Every other instruction retains its
original ALU result or PC+4 link, including every JALR. Use the existing
EX/MEM branch_taken field as the registered actual branch outcome.
When train_valid_q is set, train_index = ex_mem_w.alu_result[5:0] and
train_taken = ex_mem_w.branch_taken. No separate index/outcome payload
flops or their enables exist. Only correction_valid_q and train_valid_q
are new protocol state; branch_taken becomes a timed one-bit register.
The full ordinary pipeline reset clears payloads, and both event-valid
bits explicitly clear on reset and no-event clocks. Apply the
previous registered event to each entry's current local counter state,
without a training-read mux or fetch bypass. This is part of isolating
the verification comparator: no live EX outcome may drive fetch-PC,
queue, ID/OF or OF/EX controls, table write enables, or operand producer
eligibility. Each comparator outcome ends at correction/training
flops; architectural branch results still propagate normally. Same-index
consecutive updates must compose in order. This delayed training is
not claimed to improve accuracy and may slightly change predictions.

Remove the remaining live branch-outcome path into normal forwarding
qualification. Use ex_accept && in.ctrl.reg_write && !in.ctrl.is_illegal
&& !in.ctrl.mem_read && !in.ctrl.is_branch && !misalign_jump for normal
EX producer eligibility. Legal conditional branches never write a
register; explicitly excluding them avoids routing their alignment
trap, which depends on actual direction, through ctrl_with_trap into
OF. Keep misalign_jump for all jump link producers and retain the full
ctrl_with_trap calculation unchanged for EX/MEM and retirement. This
is necessary to isolate predictor verification, not an arithmetic
change or weakened trap rule. Preserve the registered kill gate on
normal and load producers and every architectural side effect.

During the cycle correction_valid_q is high, drive io_imemAddr from
ex_mem_w.write_data rather than the ordinary fetch-PC register. Both
mux inputs are registered full-width values; the selector is registered.
Ignore stale queue entries and offer the raw instruction at this
corrected bus address directly to ID through the empty-queue bypass.
Use that same offered PC for direction-table lookup, direct-target
addition, bus-entry PC metadata and predicted-successor generation.
Never decode target data using the stale ordinary PC. At the recovering
edge, discard old queue occupancy. If the target word is available and
accepted by ID, leave the queue empty and set ordinary PC to its
predicted successor. If available but unconsumed, retain it as the sole
new queue head and also advance PC to its predicted successor. If imem
is stalled, clear stale occupancy and install correction_target in
ordinary PC for retry. The old EX/MEM recovery payload and valid flag
must remain aligned through this complete cycle, including target
backpressure; installing the retry PC consumes the flag even if imem
is unavailable. Fetch acceptance in the correction cycle must
not depend on stale queue fullness. Reset remains highest priority.

On the original EX acceptance edge T, younger instructions may advance
speculatively while the branch enters MEM and the registered correction
becomes visible. On T+1, the target word can enter ID/OF, exactly as with
immediate parent recovery. Kill the old ID/OF word by suppressing OF
acceptance and clearing OF/EX validity. Kill the younger word already
in EX by suppressing next EX/MEM validity, normal/load forwarding
producers, branch training, further correction and divider start.
Explicitly force div_wait low for that killed word. Continue to retire
the older resolving branch normally. Do not flush the freshly accepted
target ID/OF payload. Wide invalid payloads may still clock; validity
must suppress every architectural side effect and retirement.

An accepted correction comes only from a branch or JALR, so its MEM
payload on T+1 cannot request data memory. No older dmem stall can
prevent the required kill, and an active older divider cannot coexist
with that accepted control transfer. Assert these facts. A wrong-path
DIV must be killed before launch and cannot delay fresh-target decode.
Suppress all correction/training generation while the registered kill
is active, including from a younger wrong-path branch. Keep older WB
writes and forwarding provenance intact. Backend stalls at T delay
event generation until actual EX acceptance; arbitrary imem stalls
after T retain the corrected PC and never duplicate target delivery.

Preserve exact full-width targets, alignment traps, actual RVFI next
PCs, PC+4 link writes, decoder default-illegal behavior, arithmetic,
forwarding age order, load-use handling, six-clock divider schedule,
nret=1 IO, strict retirement order and all evaluation invariants. Add
no predictor-capacity change, memory cache or pipeline stage. The
only architectural angle is complete predictor-correction registration
with target fetch on the registered correction cycle.

The final scratch prototype measures Gowin options 0/1/2 at
71.094/71.206/71.206 MHz, a 71.206 MHz median, with 4,293 LUTs,
1,001 FFs, eight LUTRAMs, six BSRAMs and six DSPs. Its option-zero
worst path is unchanged divider feedback at 19.360 ns. It passes all
eight full-RVFI selftest/random-program cosims with and without stalls.
Canonical -O3, 2K, ten-iteration CoreMark with both random bus stalls
completes with all five CRCs, the validation literal, no OOB accesses
and exactly 4,024,573 marker-bracketed cycles. This projects fitness
176.93 iter/sec, about 1.17 percent above 174.88. The integer one-percent
forecast reflects this measurement rather than the original unverified
eight-percent expectation. The measured circuit improves fitness but
does NOT clear the required 4.6-percent tournament acceptance margin.
No acceptance is claimed. Final implementation reproducibility and
the unchanged divider remain limitations; do not change arithmetic
or add an unrelated category merely to increase this predictor slot's
forecast.

Require median Gowin Fmax times canonical marker-bracketed iterations
per cycle above 182.92448 iter/sec. With unchanged 4,024,573 cycles,
median Fmax must exceed approximately 73.62 MHz. Validate all scored
placement options and unchanged unit, formal, RVFI cosim, canonical
five-CRC/UART, memory-bound and MMIO-marker checks. In particular,
retain the ten-cycle progress check and original branch/JALR-to-DIV
retirement bound; do not accept an implementation that adds a target
decode bubble or weakens a liveness assertion.

title: Bound shared divider trials to their reachable prefix widths
motivation:
The champion reaches 174.88 iterations/second at 70.381 MHz. Recent
circuits repeatedly expose divisor-to-remainder paths in the reused
radix-4 divider body. Each current cell subtracts 34-bit trial operands
with a 35-bit borrow result, although the body never needs a 34-bit
dividend window. The shared engine has processed at most 26 dividend
bits before its last body clock, so its two trial windows require only
28 and 30 bits. Keeping unreachable remainder bits in these dependent
cells wastes carry propagation and divisor routing on every body clock.

Earlier custom borrow-lookahead arithmetic and radix-16 trial expansion
regressed. Spatial width specialization with local divisor banks also
regressed and increased storage. This proposal retains the champion's
shared registers and two radix-4 cells, applying only exact width bounds
and independently prepared multiple-eligibility flags to their trials.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Specialize the existing shared divider body to its maximum reachable
prefix widths without changing its recurrence or operation schedule.
Launch still consumes four dividend bits; group zero consumes six;
groups one through five consume four each; independent terminal
publication consumes the last two. Keep the exact six-RUN-clock
real/ALTOPS completion schedule and all start/consume behavior.

At entry to the five body clocks the processed dividend lengths are
10, 14, 18, 22 and 26 bits. A restoring remainder is bounded by the
processed dividend prefix, including for divisor zero. Therefore the
first shared radix-4 cell can always form its window from
{remainder_q[25:0], quotient_q[31:30]}, a 28-bit unsigned value.
Its restored remainder is 28 bits. The second cell forms a 30-bit
window from that remainder and the next two dividend bits, yielding
a 30-bit restored remainder. Replace the respective 35-bit trial
subtractions with explicitly zero-extended 29- and 31-bit native
subtractions. Keep full 34-bit D, 2D and 3D in setup/terminal logic.

For every trial multiple M, a p-bit window may use its low p bits
only when M[33:p] is zero. Capture the three 28-bit eligibility flags
and three 30-bit eligibility flags at group zero, alongside the
existing full 3D preparation. Compute each flag from the exact full
multiple being prepared, including the NEW D+2D expression for 3D,
never the previous operation's triple_divisor_q. For D and 2D the
flags are reductions of existing registered divisor bits. Eligible
3D flags may instead use the exact constant bounds
D <= 0x05555555 and D <= 0x15555555 to avoid putting a full addition
before the flag flops. Both are unsigned comparisons of divisor_q.
Trial success is registered eligibility AND no borrow from the
corresponding shortened subtraction. Never silently truncate a
large divisor or multiple. Retain the current quotient-digit
equations and four disjoint masked-OR remainder candidates.

title: Asymmetric divider with one radix-8 body digit per clock
motivation:
The champion scores 174.88 iter/sec at 70.381 MHz and 4,024,573 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Recent vendor reports repeatedly identify divider feedback as a clock limit. Each body clock crosses two serial full-width radix-4 subtract/select cells. Extra execution clocks threaten the unchanged ten-cycle progress bound, so repartitioning existing work is preferable.

Read the structural history: r10s1 successfully introduced the six-RUN EX-only asymmetric engine; r13s1 spatial divider banks regressed to 166.95; r11s1's staged multiplier regressed to 159.50. Relevant arithmetic attempts include r11s0's fifteen-trial radix-16 body (161.35) and r8s0's serial radix-4/radix-8 groups. Neither tried one radix-8 body digit with enough narrow bootstrap work to preserve the current completion edge. LESSONS.md does not exist. Scratch multiplier-sharing, narrowed-feedback and alternating-bank probes in this proposal turn also failed to clear the champion and are excluded. A seven-trial reused body removes one dependent full-width cell with much less parallel hardware than radix-16.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Restructure only div_unit into four bits at launch, ten additional narrow bootstrap bits on the first RUN edge, five single-digit radix-8 body clocks and independent terminal three-bit publication. Exactly 4+10+5*3+3=32 bits are processed. Preserve accepted EX launch L, RUN edges L+1..L+6, READY after L+6 and EX/MEM consumption at L+7. This is one structural folding and work-repartition hypothesis, retaining the six CPU stages and nret=1.

At L retain the existing four-bit prefix computation, low twenty-eight dividend-magnitude bits, full divisor magnitude and sign/op flags. Replace the bootstrap's captured ten-bit multiples with explicitly nineteen-bit odd multiples j*m, odd j=3..31. Here m is b[13:0] for unsigned/positive b, or (14'd0-b[13:0]) modulo 2^14 for negative signed b. Capture these directly from OF/EX operand flops independently of prefix trials. Derive even multiples by shifts of captured odd multiples or m and powers of two by wiring. Size every shift/add before evaluation. Generate each odd multiple independently using shifts/adds/subtracts; compress three or more summands with carry-save logic before a final carry addition. Do not cascade newly computed multiples. These truncated-divisor multiples are ignored when full D exceeds fourteen bits.

At L+1 consume ten bits using two specialized radix-32 cells, each appending five quotient bits. The first window contains at most nine prefix bits, so use a nine-bit window and ten-bit differences; the second contains at most fourteen, so use a fourteen-bit window and fifteen-bit differences. For width w, trial j=1..31 succeeds only if every nineteen-bit multiple bit above w-1 is zero AND the zero-extended w+1-bit T-multiple subtraction has no borrow. Do not truncate large multiples into eligible trials. Set ok[0]=1, ok[32]=0 and mask[k]=ok[k]&&!ok[k+1]. Select the original window for k=0 or its matching difference for k>0 using disjoint masks and balanced OR trees, and encode the five quotient bits from masks without serial priority selection. The second cell reads only the first restored nine-bit remainder and the next five dividend bits. If divisor_q[31:14]!=0, instead append ten quotient zeros and concatenate old R4 with the next ten dividend bits. Otherwise use the two cells. Register Q={old_Q[21:0],ten_new_bits} and zero-extended R14. D=0 must emit two digits of 31 and reconstruct the prefix as remainder.

In parallel at L+1 register full unsigned thirty-five-bit 3D=D+(D<<1), 5D=D+(D<<2), and 7D=(D<<3)-D, with D widened before all operations. Prepare each independently from captured D; their arithmetic has no path into bootstrap trials. Derive 2D,4D,6D by wiring shifts of D or registered 3D. No full-width multiple preparation belongs in launch or recurring feedback.

On groups one through five, L+2..L+6, reuse exactly one radix-8 cell. Form unsigned thirty-five-bit T={R,Q[31:29]} and seven zero-extended thirty-six-bit T-jD differences. No-borrow bit 35 gives ok[j], with ok[0]=1 and ok[8]=0. Use eight masks ok[k]&&!ok[k+1], balanced masked OR remainder selection and three-bit quotient encoding; register Q={old_Q[28:0],digit} and the selected low thirty-two remainder bits. For D>0, R<D implies T<8D and restored R<D. Preserve full multiple high bits. For D=0 all trials succeed, digit seven is selected and R reconstructs the dividend. The body therefore has one dependent wide carry chain instead of two, with seven trials rather than radix-16's fifteen.

After L+6 twenty-nine bits are processed. An independent terminal radix-8 bank reads held Q/R directly and processes the last three bits, without a body-output or phase-state mux. Prepare all eight signed architectural result candidates before the late trial masks. For constant k=0..7, positive remainder is (T-kD)[31:0], negative remainder is (kD-T)[31:0], and positive quotient is {held_Q[28:0],3'(k)}. For k>0, negative quotient is {~held_Q[28:0],(3'd0-3'(k))}; for k=0 use {(29'd0-held_Q[28:0]),3'b000}. Captured operation/sign flags select within each candidate before the balanced masked OR publication. No selected digit drives a subsequent wide negate or operation mux. Retain READY state and result through delayed consume and preserve simultaneous standalone consume/relaunch semantics.

Keep the exact ALTOPS formulas and identical six-RUN schedule; never give formal a faster completion. Preserve divide-by-zero, INT_MIN/-1, dividend-only remainder sign and zero-divisor suppression of quotient negation. Reset cancels ownership and initializes preparation registers; every accepted launch overwrites each bank before use. Reject starts while busy. Keep EX-only captured operands/RVFI metadata, single publication, older-stage draining, dmem stall priority, forwarding age, load-use bubbles, branch recovery, alignment traps, decoder default-illegal and EBREAK-only SYSTEM checks, nret=1 IO, strict retirement order and every invariant. No multiplier, predictor, memory-stage or evaluation-contract change is included.

Validate actual real and ALTOPS engines against independent integer divmod, all body digits 0..7 and bootstrap digits 0..31, widths around 2^9 and 2^14, full-D bypass, overflowing multiple guards, every terminal digit/negation carry, all signs and corner cases. Retain exact six-RUN completion, eight-cycle consecutive-divide retirement, ten-cycle symbolic progress, reset/hold/relaunch assertions and all unchanged formal/RVFI cosim gates. Require canonical CoreMark CRCs, UART validation, memory bounds and marker bracketing. Inspect vendor paths through launch preparation, both narrow cells, body and terminal-to-OF publication.

Forecast eight percent fitness improvement with low confidence. This final radix-8 circuit is unimplemented and has no vendor timing measurement; the failed scratch circuits do not support an acceptance claim. The thirty-one-trial narrow bootstrap, nineteen-bit launch preparation, larger terminal bank and competing multiplier path are significant timing/area risks. At unchanged 4,024,573 CoreMark cycles, acceptance requires median Gowin Fmax above approximately 73.62 MHz and fitness above 182.92448 iter/sec. Score all placements and actual bracketed iterations/cycle without weakening any gate.

An independent Python model of the exact 4/10/15/3 partition passed 20,900 directed/random signed and unsigned quotient/remainder cases, including zero divisors and prefix-width boundaries. This checks the arithmetic partition, not SystemVerilog implementation, formal progress or vendor timing. No measured fitness gain is claimed.

title: Sixteen-entry PC-tagged target prediction for repeated JALR sites
motivation:
The champion predicts direct JAL and conditional branches but redirects
every legal aligned JALR in EX, flushing the six-stage frontend even when
the instruction repeatedly jumps to the same target. A PC-tagged table
can learn indirect call sites and returns without dependence on the
currently committed x1 value. This differs from the earlier x1-shadow
predictor and the earlier 64-entry all-control BTB: retain the successful
folded conditional predictor and cache targets only for legal JALR.
No LESSONS.md exists. Predictor history was reviewed. Scratch enlargement
to 256 direction counters saved only 0.10 percent of cycles and reduced
Fmax; moving branch comparison into OF exposed a slower forwarding path.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one fixed sixteen-entry direct-mapped JALR target predictor in IF.
Index with PC[5:2] XOR PC[9:6]. Each entry holds valid, the full word-PC
tag PC[31:2], and the full word-aligned target [31:2]. Reset only valid
bits; an invalid entry never supplies a target. Preserve all high address
bits, rather than truncating targets to the benchmark image. Lookup is
asynchronous from the registered fetch PC and registered table state.
Use old-state behavior on simultaneous lookup/update with no EX bypass.
Keep the bank small; infer compact distributed storage for tag/target
arrays where supported, with one synchronous write port and no payload
reset. Do not add a synchronous table-read stage.

Qualify a target prediction with the current raw fetched instruction:
opcode JALR, funct3 zero, aligned fetch PC, valid full-tag hit, and a
cached word-aligned target in executable RAM [0,0x00100000). The range
gate only declines speculative prediction; actual JALR resolution must
retain full RV32 addresses and all existing bounds checks. Do not make
predictions from stale PC tags for non-JALR or illegal encodings. On a
qualified hit select the cached target as the fetch successor. Otherwise
preserve the existing conditional/JAL prediction and sequential JALR.
Advance only under the existing bus/queue fetch-acceptance rule.

Carry a separate predicted_jalr_valid bit and thirty-bit predicted_jalr
target atomically with the instruction through both fetch entries,
empty bypass, IF/ID, ID/OF and OF/EX. Keep predicted_taken exclusively
for existing direct-control direction prediction. The target represents
the exact full 32-bit address with two known zero alignment bits.
Preserve prediction metadata through holds; validity kills discard its
authority. Never verify a queued instruction against the table's newer
contents, and do not use generation counters instead of the saved target.

In EX compute actual JALR normally from the captured fully forwarded rs1
plus immediate, clear bit zero and retain the existing alignment trap.
For an accepted legal nontrapping JALR, redirect exactly when it had no
target prediction or its actual target differs from the saved target.
A correct prediction causes no flush and retains normal PC+4 link writes.
A wrong target redirects to the exact actual target and discards all
younger words. If a predicted JALR resolves to a misaligned target,
flush its speculative successor and recover to the existing sequential
PC+4 trap successor while suppressing the link write. An unpredicted
trapping JALR retains today's sequential behavior. Gate every correction
with current EX acceptance so older dmem holds cannot replay it.

Train the indexed entry exactly once from each accepted legal aligned
JALR whose actual target lies in executable RAM, capturing its full PC
tag and actual target. Refresh a matching entry on changed targets and
replace on tag conflict; no confidence counters or speculative updates
are needed. Never train conditional branches, JAL, illegal instructions,
trapped targets, wrong-path words, held instructions or bubbles. Keep
JALR training separate from the unchanged BHT training interface.
A resolving misprediction still trains its own accepted actual target.
Reset overrides all updates. A table miss is ordinary unpredicted JALR
execution and must never prevent forward progress.

Preserve the folded-PC 64x2 conditional predictor, local saturation,
weakly-taken reset, exact aligned BRANCH/JAL predecode, immediate EX
correction latency, two-entry queue, arithmetic and pipeline depth.
Retain nret=1, all top-level ports, decoder default-illegal behavior,
full RVFI operands and actual next PCs, strict retirement order, all
memory handshakes, held-WB forwarding, wrong-path DIV/store suppression,
ten-cycle progress and unchanged correctness checks.

The intended benefit is eliminating repeat JALR flushes. The forecast
is two percent with low confidence: target changes, table conflicts,
full-target metadata and the new equality check can erase the savings.
No vendor timing improvement or tournament acceptance is claimed for
this final architecture. Require median Gowin Fmax times canonical
marker-bracketed iterations/cycle above 182.92448 iter/sec to replace
the champion, together with all five canonical CRCs, validation UART,
memory bounds, formal and full-RVFI cosim checks. Do not mix a divider,
cache, forwarding or conditional-predictor change into this slot.
